requirements.title: PowerMode variants distinct
requirements.text: PowerMode::Normal, StandBy, Sleep, Unpowered are pairwise distinct, and as_str() gives each a distinct name
requirements.tc18: §12.4 ("The RC Server may support different power modes"), TC18.txt L2644

requirements.title: Ordinary power-mode transition shape
requirements.text: is_power_mode_transition_defined allows exactly the two ordinary (non-start-up) edges of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.4 Figure 17 'power and operation modes' (p.46): Normal->StandBy ('Go to StandBy') and Normal->Sleep ('Go to Sleep'). Every other ordered pair is undefined, including StandBy<->Sleep in both directions (Figure 17 draws no edge between the two low-power modes; each is reached from and returns to Normal only), the two wake-up edges back to Normal (start-up paths owned by try_hot_start/try_cold_start), any pair naming Unpowered, and staying in the same mode
requirements.tc18: §12.4 Figure 18 ("power and operation modes") -- note: this crate's own text/doc-comments call it "Figure 17", a stale figure number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), Figure 17 is §12.3's RC-Server-lifecycle-states diagram, while the power/operation-modes diagram is Figure 18. Independently verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.55, which draws Normal->StandBy labelled "Go to StandBy", Normal->Sleep labelled "Go to Sleep", and no edge between StandBy and Sleep, TC18.txt L2658

requirements.title: PowerModeGateInput requires both flags
requirements.text: is_power_mode_gate_satisfied returns true only when both all_endpoints_idle and no_pending_response are true
requirements.tc18: §12.5 ("The RC Server will reject requests to enter sleep or standby mode and send an error message with error code = REQUEST_CANCELED, when - The wake-up event register (wup_status) is not cleared - At least one EP is not idle - In at least one responder queue there is a message pending for transmission."), TC18.txt L2703-2708

requirements.title: try_enter_power_mode gates on shape and idleness
requirements.text: try_enter_power_mode returns Ok(to) only when is_power_mode_transition_defined(from, to) and is_power_mode_gate_satisfied(gate) both hold, and Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) otherwise
requirements.tc18: §12.5 ("The RC Server will reject requests to enter sleep or standby mode and send an error message with error code = REQUEST_CANCELED, when - The wake-up event register (wup_status) is not cleared - At least one EP is not idle - In at least one responder queue there is a message pending for transmission."), TC18.txt L2703-2708

requirements.title: shutdown_to_unpowered is unconditional
requirements.text: shutdown_to_unpowered always returns PowerMode::Unpowered from any of Normal, StandBy, or Sleep, with no gate applied

requirements.title: WakeUp handshake advances Idle -> RequestSent -> Acknowledged only
requirements.text: send_wakeup_request succeeds only from Idle (to RequestSent); acknowledge_wakeup_request succeeds only from RequestSent (to Acknowledged); both return Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) from any other state; default state is Idle
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("the RC Server will send via the responder stream which is configured for the original standby request a repetitive response to the sleep request with a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The message will be repeated until a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client is received."), TC18.txt L2674-2676

requirements.title: is_wakeup_handshake_complete true only for Acknowledged
requirements.text: is_wakeup_handshake_complete returns true only for WakeUpHandshakeState::Acknowledged and false for Idle and RequestSent
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("the RC Server will send via the responder stream which is configured for the original standby request a repetitive response to the sleep request with a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The message will be repeated until a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client is received."), TC18.txt L2674-2676

requirements.title: Power-mode functions never panic
requirements.text: try_enter_power_mode, shutdown_to_unpowered, try_cold_start, try_hot_start, send_wakeup_request, acknowledge_wakeup_request, and is_wakeup_handshake_complete do not panic across a sampled cross-product of PowerMode, PowerModeGateInput, and WakeUpHandshakeState inputs

requirements.title: try_cold_start admits both TC18 cold-start origins (Unpowered and Sleep)
requirements.text: TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.4.1 'Power-On / Wake-Up / Start-Up behavior' (p.46) defines the cold start with two origins — 'a cold start (after power-on or wake-up from sleep)' — and §12.4 Figure 17 labels both the Unpowered->Normal and the Sleep->Normal arrow 'Cold start'. try_cold_start therefore returns Ok(PowerMode::Normal) when from is PowerMode::Unpowered or PowerMode::Sleep and gate satisfies is_power_mode_gate_satisfied, and Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) otherwise — including from PowerMode::Normal, from PowerMode::StandBy (whose resume is the hot start, REQ-PWRSTART-002), and from a valid origin whose gate is unsatisfied. No WakeUp handshake gates this path: §12.4.1 attaches the handshake to the 'Hot-start-up procedure' only
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("There are two types of start-up: a cold start (after power-on or wake-up from sleep) and a hot start (=wake-up from StandBy)"), TC18.txt L2663-2664 -- note: this requirement's own text cites this section as "(p.46)" and the Cold-start arrows as "§12.4 Figure 17"; in the current TC18.txt (RC5) §12.4.1 is on p.55 and the power/operation-modes diagram is Figure 18 (independently confirmed against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf, whose Figure 18 draws both Unpowered->Normal and Sleep->Normal arrows labelled "Cold start")

requirements.title: try_hot_start requires StandBy origin, acknowledged handshake, and gate
requirements.text: TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.4.1 (p.46) defines the hot start with exactly one origin — 'a hot start (=wake-up from StandBy)' — drawn in §12.4 Figure 17 as the single arrow labelled 'Hot start', and it is §12.4.1's 'Hot-start-up procedure' that specifies the repeated WakeUp message awaiting 'a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client', which WakeUpHandshakeState models. try_hot_start therefore returns Ok(PowerMode::Normal) only when from == PowerMode::StandBy, wakeup == WakeUpHandshakeState::Acknowledged, and gate satisfies is_power_mode_gate_satisfied; Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) otherwise, including from PowerMode::Sleep even with an acknowledged handshake (that origin is a cold start, REQ-PWRSTART-001)
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("the RC Server will send via the responder stream which is configured for the original standby request a repetitive response to the sleep request with a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The message will be repeated until a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client is received."), TC18.txt L2674-2676 -- note: this requirement's own text cites this section as "(p.46)" and the Hot-start arrow as "§12.4 Figure 17"; in the current TC18.txt (RC5) §12.4.1 is on p.55 and the power/operation-modes diagram (single StandBy->Normal arrow labelled "Hot start") is Figure 18

requirements.title: power_mode_gate_from_request_states composes RequestLifecycleState
requirements.text: power_mode_gate_from_request_states returns a PowerModeGateInput with both fields true iff every crate::request::RequestLifecycleState entry in the given slice is Finalized (an empty slice is vacuously idle); any Pending, Started, or UnderExecution entry makes both fields false

requirements.title: NTSCF frame identifies itself by subtype
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame's output starts with avtp::NTSCF_SUBTYPE (0x82, TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22)) with the sv bit set, via its delegation to encode_ntscf_header; encode_ntscf_frame rejects an acf_payload exceeding the 11-bit ntscf_data_length field width (Figure 6, bits 13-23) with Err(InvalidSize)
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF frame sequence_num and stream_id pass through unchanged
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame/decode_ntscf_frame round-trip the caller-supplied sequence_num and stream_id unchanged, exactly as decode_ntscf_header recovers them
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF frame payload is opaque to the composition step
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame/decode_ntscf_frame carry the ACF payload bytes verbatim without parsing them as any specific ACF message type — that remains acf::decode_acf_abb/decode_acf_gbb's job on the split payload decode_ntscf_frame returns

requirements.title: NTSCF frame length is header length plus payload length
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame's output is always exactly avtp::NTSCF_HEADER_LEN + acf_payload.len() bytes, with no padding or reserved gap inserted — TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) places acf_payload_data immediately after stream_id, at octet 12
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF frame encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame(stream_id, sequence_num, payload) followed by decode_ntscf_frame() recovers the same header fields and the same payload bytes, for both a non-empty and an empty payload

requirements.title: UdpTransport/TlsBridge send ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB over NTSCF frames
requirements.text: UdpTransport::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb and TlsBridge::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb each wrap their message in encode_ntscf_frame, and decode the response the same way, recovering the original message's fields
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("The corresponding NTSCF header in version 0 shall be used for RCP requests which shall be executed as soon as possible or under request specific conditions as well as for responses and acknowledge."), TC18.txt L1130-1132

requirements.title: NTSCF frame payload size limit
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_frame rejects an acf_payload longer than avtp::NTSCF_DATA_LENGTH_MAX (0x07FF, the 11-bit ntscf_data_length field width at bits 13-23 of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22)) with Err(InvalidSize)
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: Wrong-subtype NTSCF frame rejected
requirements.text: decode_ntscf_frame propagates decode_ntscf_header's own rejection of a frame whose leading subtype byte is not avtp::NTSCF_SUBTYPE

requirements.title: NTSCF frame functions never panic on arbitrary/truncated input
requirements.text: decode_ntscf_frame never panics for input shorter than avtp::NTSCF_HEADER_LEN (12 octets per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22); returns Err(ShortFrame)) or for arbitrary byte content at any length, matching the fuzz-style discipline the deleted wire.rs originally established (carried forward by fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_wire_decode.rs, repointed at this function)

requirements.title: Requests encoded as NTSCF-headed AVTPDU frames
requirements.text: UdpTransport::send_acf_abb/send_acf_gbb encode their message via acf::encode_acf_abb/encode_acf_gbb and avtp::encode_ntscf_frame, and decode the response via avtp::decode_ntscf_frame and acf::decode_acf_abb/decode_acf_gbb, rejecting a zero timeout with Err(Timeout) before ever touching the socket

requirements.title: resolve_endpoint routes EP0 vs. device endpoint

requirements.title: Protocol enum
requirements.text: The relay module shall define a Protocol enum matching RELAY spec §3 identifiers, serializing as its integer value

requirements.title: Message envelope
requirements.text: The relay module shall define a Message type matching the RELAY spec §4 universal envelope, with base64-encoded payload

requirements.title: BackPressurePolicy
requirements.text: The relay module shall define a BackPressurePolicy enum (DropNewest/DropOldest/Block) per RELAY spec §14, defaulting to DropNewest

requirements.title: SubscriberOptions
requirements.text: The relay module shall define a SubscriberOptions type per RELAY spec §18.3 with a channel_depth default of 64

requirements.title: relay::Error sentinels
requirements.text: The relay module shall define the four mandatory RELAY error sentinels (Closed, NotConnected, Timeout, PayloadTooLarge) per §5.1, mutually distinct

requirements.title: Context
requirements.text: The relay module shall define a Context type carrying an optional deadline per RELAY spec §18.3

requirements.title: relay::Node trait
requirements.text: The relay module shall define an async Node trait (protocol/send/subscribe/close) per RELAY spec §10.1

requirements.title: relay::Caller trait
requirements.text: The relay module shall define an async Caller trait extending Node with call() per RELAY spec §10.2

requirements.title: Base64 payload serde
requirements.text: Message and Command/Response/Status payload fields shall serialize as base64 strings per RELAY spec §15.1, matching Go's []byte JSON marshalling

requirements.title: AcfAbbMessage response ToMessage()
requirements.text: to_message() shall convert an addressed ACF_ABB response to a relay::Message per RELAY spec §15.7.5 (stream_id+byte_bus_id encoded as ID, op surfaced via the rcp.op meta key, payload)

requirements.title: Message.FromMessage() to AcfAbbMessage
requirements.text: from_message() shall convert a relay::Message to an addressed ACF_ABB request per RELAY spec §15.7.5 (stream_id+byte_bus_id decoded from ID, op/read_size from meta keys), returning InvalidParameter for a malformed ID or an unrecognized rcp.op value

requirements.title: AcfAbbMessage response.ToMessage() reply half
requirements.text: response_to_message() shall convert an addressed ACF_ABB response to a relay::Message per RELAY spec §15.7.5 (Caller.Call reply half), matching to_message()'s own conversion

requirements.title: Adapt()
requirements.text: adapt() shall wrap an RcServer as a relay::Node/Caller per RELAY spec §10.3, addressed by (StreamId, byte_bus_id), dispatching blocking RcServer calls via spawn_blocking, honoring an already-expired Context as Timeout, tracking its own closed state since RcServer has no open/closed connection concept of its own, and returning an immediately-closed channel from subscribe() since RcServer has no live-notification mechanism to forward

requirements.title: Caller.Call()
requirements.text: The Adapt() adapter's call() shall dispatch an addressed ACF_ABB request derived from the request Message against the wrapped RcServer and return its response as a relay::Message per RELAY spec §10.2/§15.7.5

requirements.title: Endpoint-address Message.id encoding
requirements.text: format_endpoint_id()/parse_endpoint_id() shall encode/decode a (StreamId, byte_bus_id) pair to/from a relay::Message.id string, rejecting malformed input with InvalidParameter rather than panicking

requirements.title: NtscfHeader field model
requirements.text: NtscfHeader models sequence_num, ntscf_data_length, and stream_id for the NTSCF AVTPDU header variant — the three named fields TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) defines, with no others.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF header encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_ntscf_header emits the exact 12-octet layout of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22): octet 0 subtype, octet 1 sv(1)|version(3)|r(1)|ntscf_data_length[10:8](3), octet 2 ntscf_data_length[7:0], octet 3 sequence_num, octets 4-11 stream_id big-endian — with no reserved gap anywhere. decode_ntscf_header of that output recovers the original header, and an ntscf_data_length above the 11-bit field width (bits 13-23 of the first quadlet) is rejected with InvalidSize.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF subtype and sv bit
requirements.text: Encoded NTSCF headers carry subtype 0x82 and set the sv bit, identifying the AVTPDU as NTSCF with a valid stream_id. Both values are read from TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) ('subtype(0x82)', bits 0-7; 'sv', bit 8) and confirmed by the worked example in TC18 Figure 20 (p.79).
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF decode rejects malformed input
requirements.text: decode_ntscf_header rejects frames shorter than avtp::NTSCF_HEADER_LEN (12 octets, the header length TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 6 (NTSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) specifies), a subtype other than 0x82, or an unset sv bit.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: NTSCF decode never panics
requirements.text: decode_ntscf_header never panics on arbitrary or truncated input

requirements.title: NTSCF decode robust across input lengths
requirements.text: decode_ntscf_header never panics across a swept range of arbitrary input lengths and contents

requirements.title: TscfHeader field model
requirements.text: TscfHeader models every field of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 5 (TSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) explicitly: version, mr, tv, sequence_num, tu, stream_id, avtp_timestamp, stream_data_length, and the two reserved regions (reserved0/reserved1, decode-only). tv is a stored wire bit, never derived from avtp_timestamp; sv is always set on encode and required on decode.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: TSCF header encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_tscf_header emits the exact 24-octet layout of TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 5 (TSCF-Header Version 0, p.22): octet 0 subtype, octet 1 sv(1)|version(3)|mr(1)|rsv(2)|tv(1), octet 2 sequence_num, octet 3 reserved(7)|tu(1), octets 4-11 stream_id, octets 12-15 avtp_timestamp, octets 16-19 reserved, octets 20-21 stream_data_length as a full 16-bit big-endian field, octets 22-23 reserved. decode_tscf_header of that output recovers the original header. Because stream_data_length's wire field is a full 16 bits (avtp::TSCF_DATA_LENGTH_MAX == u16::MAX), every representable value is in range and the call never returns InvalidSize.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: TSCF subtype and sv bit
requirements.text: Encoded TSCF headers carry subtype 0x05 and set the sv bit, identifying the AVTPDU as TSCF with a valid stream_id, distinct from the NTSCF subtype. The value is read from TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 5 (TSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) ('subtype(0x05)', bits 0-7) and confirmed by the worked example in TC18 Figure 19 (p.79); it is unrelated to NTSCF's 0x82 and is the smaller of the two. The tv bit (Figure 5, bit 15) is taken from TscfHeader::tv verbatim, so a valid timestamp of 0 and an invalid non-zero timestamp are both representable.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: TSCF decode rejects malformed input
requirements.text: decode_tscf_header rejects frames shorter than avtp::TSCF_HEADER_LEN (24 octets, the header length TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.1 Figure 5 (TSCF-Header Version 0, p.22) specifies), a subtype other than 0x05, or an unset sv bit.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: TSCF decode never panics
requirements.text: decode_tscf_header never panics on arbitrary or truncated input

requirements.title: TSCF decode robust across input lengths
requirements.text: decode_tscf_header never panics across a swept range of arbitrary input lengths and contents

requirements.title: TimeSyncCapability / HeaderVariant / HeaderSelection model
requirements.text: TimeSyncCapability models a receiving server's time-synchronization capability (Capable/Incapable), HeaderVariant tags a decoded header as Ntscf or Tscf, and HeaderSelection reports select_header_variant's disposition (Accept, IgnorePresentationTime, Drop)

requirements.title: TSCF dropped at a time-sync-incapable server
requirements.text: select_header_variant returns Ok(HeaderSelection::Drop) for a TSCF-subtyped AVTPDU when the receiving server has no time-synchronization support and the TscfFallback policy is Drop (the default), without decoding the remainder of the header and without an error (so no response is sent).
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140

requirements.title: TSCF accepted at a time-sync-capable server
requirements.text: select_header_variant decodes a TSCF-subtyped AVTPDU into HeaderSelection::Accept(HeaderVariant::Tscf) when the receiving server supports time synchronization, regardless of TscfFallback policy, delegating to decode_tscf_header for the header body
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140

requirements.title: NTSCF always accepted regardless of time-sync capability
requirements.text: select_header_variant decodes an NTSCF-subtyped AVTPDU into HeaderSelection::Accept(HeaderVariant::Ntscf) regardless of the receiving server's time-synchronization capability or TscfFallback policy

requirements.title: select_header_variant never panics on malformed input
requirements.text: select_header_variant never panics on empty, truncated, or unrecognized-subtype input, returning ShortFrame or Other instead

requirements.title: ByteMessageInfo field model
requirements.text: ByteMessageInfo models the ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB shared header fields (acf_msg_length, pad, mtv, byte_bus_id, evt as an ack flag plus 3-bit sub_opcode, hs, cs, transaction_num, op, rsp, err, ms) plus a documented, non-ambiguous convention for the dual-purpose read_size/segment_num field rather than a single ambiguous field
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: byte_message_info encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_byte_message_info followed by decode_byte_message_info recovers the original ByteMessageInfo, including at the 11-bit byte_bus_id/acf_msg_length maxima and the 3-bit evt.sub_opcode maximum
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: byte_message_info encode rejects out-of-range fields
requirements.text: encode_byte_message_info rejects an acf_msg_length or byte_bus_id wider than 11 bits and an evt.sub_opcode wider than 3 bits
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: byte_message_info decode never panics
requirements.text: decode_byte_message_info never panics on truncated or arbitrary input, across a swept range of input lengths

requirements.title: ReadSizeOrSegment selected by the op bit
requirements.text: ByteMessageInfo::read_size/segment_num select the ReadSizeOrSegment field's read_size vs. segment_num interpretation by the op flag, returning None on the side op does not indicate, rather than an unconditional value under either interpretation
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1208-1236

requirements.title: AcfAbbMessage field model
requirements.text: AcfAbbMessage models an ACF_ABB message as a ByteMessageInfo plus an opaque payload only, with no timestamp field of any kind and no reserved gap sized for one
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_ABB encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_acf_abb followed by decode_acf_abb recovers the original message, and the encoded length is always exactly the discriminant byte plus byte_message_info plus the payload, with no timestamp region inserted
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_ABB acf_msg_type discriminant
requirements.text: Encoded ACF_ABB messages carry the acf_msg_type discriminant 0x0E as their leading byte
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_ABB decode rejects malformed input
requirements.text: decode_acf_abb rejects empty/too-short input and input whose leading byte is not the ACF_ABB discriminant 0x0E, distinguishing the ACF_GBB discriminant 0x0D with a specific hint

requirements.title: ACF_ABB decode never panics
requirements.text: decode_acf_abb never panics on arbitrary or truncated input, across a swept range of input lengths

requirements.title: AcfGbbMessage field model
requirements.text: AcfGbbMessage models an ACF_GBB message as a ByteMessageInfo plus a 64-bit message_timestamp plus an opaque payload; message_timestamp is carried/round-tripped as a raw value only, with full rollover/fallback semantics deferred to the Timestamp Semantics checklist item
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_GBB encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: encode_acf_gbb followed by decode_acf_gbb recovers the original message, including the full 64-bit message_timestamp range, and the encoded length is always exactly the discriminant byte plus byte_message_info plus the 8-byte timestamp plus the payload
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_GBB acf_msg_type discriminant
requirements.text: Encoded ACF_GBB messages carry the acf_msg_type discriminant 0x0D as their leading byte
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Table 17 ("Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"), TC18.txt L2242-2266

requirements.title: ACF_GBB decode rejects malformed input
requirements.text: decode_acf_gbb rejects empty/too-short input and input whose leading byte is not the ACF_GBB discriminant 0x0D, distinguishing the ACF_ABB discriminant 0x0E with a specific hint

requirements.title: ACF_GBB decode never panics
requirements.text: decode_acf_gbb never panics on arbitrary or truncated input, across a swept range of input lengths

requirements.title: StreamId construct/parse model
requirements.text: StreamId decomposes an opaque 64-bit AVTP stream_id into a sender MAC address and a locally-assigned unique-id suffix (and composes the reverse), via build_stream_id/parse_stream_id and the StreamId::to_u64/from_u64/From/Into wrappers around them
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 Table 18 ("stream_id = streamMAC + unique_id", streamMAC: 6 bytes, unique_id: 2 bytes), TC18.txt L2750 -- note: this crate's own doc comment (src/avtp.rs) cites this as "Table 16", a stale table number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), this discovery-request field table is Table 18 (and the paired discovery-response table it also cites as "Table 17" is actually Table 19); the discovery tables state the streamMAC/unique_id split for the discovery-specific don't-care/fixed values, which this crate's own doc comment already treats as the reconciliation source for the general stream_id encoding convention

requirements.title: stream_id round-trip
requirements.text: build_stream_id composed with parse_stream_id recovers the original sender MAC address and unique-id suffix, including the all-zero and all-0xFF extremes

requirements.title: stream_id bit layout
requirements.text: build_stream_id places the sender MAC address in the upper 48 bits of the composed stream_id (most-significant octet first) and the unique-id suffix in the lower 16 bits
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 Table 18 ("stream_id = streamMAC + unique_id", streamMAC: 6 bytes, unique_id: 2 bytes), TC18.txt L2750 -- note: this crate's own doc comment (src/avtp.rs) cites this as "Table 16", a stale table number: in the current TC18.txt (RC5), this discovery-request field table is Table 18

requirements.title: parse_stream_id never panics
requirements.text: parse_stream_id never panics for any u64 input value, across a swept range including the extremes

requirements.title: StreamId interop with NTSCF/TSCF opaque field
requirements.text: A StreamId composed to u64 and carried through NtscfHeader::stream_id or TscfHeader::stream_id's encode/decode round trip parses back to the original StreamId

requirements.title: EndpointTable / EndpointId model
requirements.text: EndpointTable models a (stream_id, byte_bus_id) -> EndpointId lookup as a map keyed first by StreamId and then, per stream, by byte_bus_id, so that byte_bus_id's keyspace is scoped to a single stream rather than shared globally across all streams
requirements.tc18: §13.1 ("The byte_bus_id is only unique in the context of a STREAM_ID and requests are only passed to the endpoint if both match."), TC18.txt L3898-3899

requirements.title: EndpointTable::register enforces per-pair uniqueness and field width
requirements.text: EndpointTable::register rejects a byte_bus_id wider than the 11-bit field width shared with ByteMessageInfo::byte_bus_id with RcpError::InvalidSize, and rejects re-registering an already-registered (stream_id, byte_bus_id) pair with RcpError::EndpointAlreadyRegistered without modifying the existing registration, while permitting the same byte_bus_id to be registered independently under a different stream_id

requirements.title: EndpointTable::lookup resolves the stream-relative pair
requirements.text: EndpointTable::lookup resolves a (stream_id, byte_bus_id) pair to the EndpointId registered under that exact pair, returning None when either component does not match a registered entry, and never returning an endpoint registered under a different stream_id even when byte_bus_id matches
requirements.tc18: §13.1 ("The byte_bus_id is only unique in the context of a STREAM_ID and requests are only passed to the endpoint if both match."), TC18.txt L3898-3899

requirements.title: EndpointTable::lookup never panics
requirements.text: EndpointTable::lookup never panics for any (stream_id, byte_bus_id) input, on an empty table or a populated one, across a swept range including the all-zero and all-0xFF/u16::MAX extremes

requirements.title: Echo-back rule model
requirements.text: The echo-back rule (a response/ack must carry the same byte_bus_id it was received under) is modeled as a pair of plain functions over already-decoded ByteMessageInfo values, build_response_info and verify_echo_back, with no dependency on StreamId/EndpointTable addressing machinery
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("Response(s) and acknowledge(s) are associated to the requests by the byte_bus_id and transaction number."), TC18.txt L3610

requirements.title: build_response_info echoes byte_bus_id and sets rsp
requirements.text: build_response_info returns a response ByteMessageInfo with byte_bus_id copied from the request and rsp forced true, leaving every other field of the caller-supplied response template unchanged
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("Response(s) and acknowledge(s) are associated to the requests by the byte_bus_id and transaction number."), TC18.txt L3610

requirements.title: verify_echo_back accepts matching and rejects mismatched byte_bus_id
requirements.text: verify_echo_back returns Ok when response.byte_bus_id equals request.byte_bus_id regardless of the response.rsp flag, and returns Err(RcpError::EchoBackMismatch) when byte_bus_id differs
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("Response(s) and acknowledge(s) are associated to the requests by the byte_bus_id and transaction number."), TC18.txt L3610

requirements.title: Echo-back rule functions never panic
requirements.text: build_response_info and verify_echo_back never panic for any combination of ByteMessageInfo field values, across a swept range of byte_bus_id inputs

requirements.title: AvtpTimestamp/MessageTimestamp are distinct types
requirements.text: AvtpTimestamp (wrapping TscfHeader::avtp_timestamp's raw u32) and MessageTimestamp (wrapping AcfGbbMessage::message_timestamp's raw u64) are modeled as two distinct newtypes with no shared trait or cross-type comparison, so the two fields' distinct widths and distinct rollover periods can never be confused with one another

requirements.title: AvtpTimestamp wraparound-aware comparison
requirements.text: AvtpTimestamp::wrapping_delta/is_after compare two 32-bit timestamps correctly across their rollover boundary, reporting a small delta when one value has just wrapped past the other rather than a large one

requirements.title: MessageTimestamp wraparound-aware comparison
requirements.text: MessageTimestamp::wrapping_delta/is_after compare two 64-bit timestamps correctly across their own, independent rollover boundary, using the same wraparound convention as AvtpTimestamp but over a distinct, much longer period

requirements.title: Timestamp validity comes from the tv/mtv bit, not the raw value
requirements.text: TimestampMeaning::from_valid_bit maps a wire validity bit (TSCF tv / ACF_GBB mtv) to TimestampMeaning::Timed (bit set) or TimestampMeaning::Untimed (bit clear) independent of the raw timestamp value, so a raw value of 0 is a valid timestamp when its validity bit is set; TscfHeader::timestamp_meaning applies this to a decoded TSCF header, ignoring tu (TC18 §13.3).
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("For requests sent in an AVTPDU having a TSCF header with the time stamp marked as invalid (i.e. tv = 0), the timestamp is ignored."), TC18.txt L4038-4039

requirements.title: Round trip / interop with the raw wire fields
requirements.text: AvtpTimestamp/MessageTimestamp round-trip through their raw u32/u64 values (including via From/Into) and interoperate with values sourced from TscfHeader::avtp_timestamp and AcfGbbMessage::message_timestamp without either header/message struct's field type changing

requirements.title: Timestamp semantics never panic
requirements.text: AvtpTimestamp and MessageTimestamp's wrapping_delta/is_after never panic for any combination of raw input values, across a swept range including the all-zero, all-1s, and half-rollover-period extremes

requirements.title: RcServerState three-state model and numeric encoding
requirements.text: RcServerState models the three named RC Server lifecycle states (HwUnconfigured, HwConfigured, RcpConfigured) with wire-level byte encodings 0x00/0x55/0xAA respectively, defaults to HwUnconfigured, and round-trips every valid encoding through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 ("RC Server functional configuration"), TC18.txt L4388-4390

requirements.title: RcServerState::from_u8 rejects unrecognized bytes
requirements.text: RcServerState::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::Other) for every byte other than 0x00, 0x55, and 0xAA, without panicking
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 ("svr_lifecycle_state: 0x00 HW_UNCONFIGURED / 0x55 HW_CONFIGURED / 0xAA RCP_CONFIGURED"), TC18.txt L4388-4390

requirements.title: Per-state register category reachability rule
requirements.text: is_register_reachable models RegisterCategory::General and RegisterCategory::HwConfig as reachable in every RcServerState, and RegisterCategory::RcpConfig as reachable only in HwConfigured and RcpConfigured, not in HwUnconfigured

requirements.title: check_register_reachable enforces the reachability rule
requirements.text: check_register_reachable returns Ok(()) exactly when is_register_reachable would return true for the same (state, category) pair, and Err(RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess) otherwise

requirements.title: Lifecycle decode and reachability checks never panic
requirements.text: RcServerState::from_u8 never panics across the full 0..=255 byte range, and is_register_reachable/check_register_reachable never panic for any RcServerState/RegisterCategory pair

requirements.title: Transition guard defines exactly the five modeled transitions
requirements.text: is_transition_defined returns true exactly for the five transitions c-RCP rcp_lifecycle_transition models -- (HwUnconfigured, HwConfigured), (HwConfigured, RcpConfigured), (RcpConfigured, HwConfigured), (HwConfigured, HwUnconfigured), (RcpConfigured, HwUnconfigured) -- and false for same-state pairs and for (HwUnconfigured, RcpConfigured); RcServerState::try_transition succeeds on each of those five when its writer, idleness and plausibility guards pass, and returns LifecycleError::InvalidTransition for (HwUnconfigured, RcpConfigured)

requirements.title: try_transition enforces the structured plausibility guards
requirements.text: RcServerState::try_transition gates HwUnconfigured -> HwConfigured on lifecycle::check_hw_cfg and HwConfigured -> RcpConfigured on lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg over a PlausibilitySnapshot, returning LifecycleError::HwCfgInconsistent / LifecycleError::RcpCfgInconsistent (and leaving the state unchanged) when the check fails, including for a None snapshot

requirements.title: try_transition rejects unmodeled transitions and never panics
requirements.text: RcServerState::try_transition returns Err(LifecycleError::InvalidTransition) for (HwUnconfigured, RcpConfigured) regardless of writer, snapshot or idleness, returns Ok(self) for a same-state request, and never panics for any (from, to, snapshot, writer, idle) input; its full result table matches c-RCP rcp_lifecycle_transition byte-for-byte (testdata/c_rcp_lifecycle_golden.txt)

requirements.title: LockPolicy per-category (W vs W*) assignment
requirements.text: lock_policy maps RegisterCategory::General to None (never writable), RegisterCategory::HwConfig to Some(LockPolicy::WStar), and RegisterCategory::RcpConfig to Some(LockPolicy::W); is_register_writable composes that mapping with is_register_reachable so General is never writable, HwConfig is writable while reachable except in RcpConfigured, and RcpConfig is writable whenever reachable including in RcpConfigured

requirements.title: check_register_writable enforces the write-lock rule and distinguishes unreachable from locked
requirements.text: check_register_writable returns Ok(()) exactly when is_register_writable would return true for the same (state, category) pair, Err(RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess) if the category is not reachable at all in that state, and Err(RcpError::LockedMemAccess) if it is reachable but write-locked

requirements.title: Write-lock checks never panic
requirements.text: lock_policy, is_register_writable, and check_register_writable never panic for any RcServerState/RegisterCategory pair

requirements.title: Demotion paths are guarded by writer authorization and idleness
requirements.text: RcServerState::try_transition admits HwConfigured -> HwUnconfigured for a discovery-stream, root-client or valid-stream-association writer, RcpConfigured -> HwConfigured for a root-client or valid-stream-association writer, and RcpConfigured -> HwUnconfigured for the root client only, each only when all_other_eps_idle is true (LifecycleError::Unauthorized / LifecycleError::EpsNotIdle otherwise); none of the demotions consults the plausibility snapshot

requirements.title: EP0 reserved byte_bus_id recognition
requirements.text: EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID is 0, and is_ep0_address returns true iff byte_bus_id equals EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID, for every representable byte_bus_id value, without panicking
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("For configuration purposes the RC Server itself is also treated as an endpoint. It may have within each configured stream_id an own byte_bus_id, which is zero as a default."), TC18.txt L3594-3595

requirements.title: EP0 vs. device-endpoint routing is decided before and independent of EndpointTable
requirements.text: route_byte_bus_id returns RequestRoute::Ep0 iff byte_bus_id is EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID and RequestRoute::DeviceEndpoint otherwise, for every representable byte_bus_id value, without panicking and without taking or consulting an EndpointTable; the routing decision for EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID is unchanged regardless of whether EndpointTable has an entry registered at that byte_bus_id
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("For configuration purposes the RC Server itself is also treated as an endpoint. It may have within each configured stream_id an own byte_bus_id, which is zero as a default."), TC18.txt L3594-3595

requirements.title: EP0 access direction derived from ByteMessageInfo::op
requirements.text: access_kind returns Ep0AccessKind::Read when info.op is false and Ep0AccessKind::Write when info.op is true
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1 ("A response with pay load data read from the EP is given, if requested by op=0 (read request) after the request has been executed."), TC18.txt L3604-3605

requirements.title: EP0 read access composes with lifecycle register reachability
requirements.text: check_ep0_access with an info whose op is false returns the same result as lifecycle::check_register_reachable for the same (state, category) pair, for every RcServerState/RegisterCategory combination

requirements.title: EP0 write access composes with lifecycle register writability and distinguishes unreachable from locked
requirements.text: check_ep0_access with an info whose op is true returns the same result as lifecycle::check_register_writable for the same (state, category) pair, for every RcServerState/RegisterCategory combination, including reporting RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess (not LockedMemAccess) for an unreachable category and RcpError::LockedMemAccess for a reachable but write-locked category

requirements.title: EP0 access check never panics
requirements.text: check_ep0_access never panics for any RcServerState/RegisterCategory/op combination

requirements.title: Root-client identity check
requirements.text: is_root_client(root_client, stream) returns true iff root_client is Some(stream), and false when root_client is None or Some of a different stream
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 ("The svr_root_client_index is an index that selects the request stream which is in HW_CONFIGURED still allowed to access all registers of the register map."), TC18.txt L4400-4401

requirements.title: Root-client-aware EP0 reads are unaffected by root-client status
requirements.text: check_ep0_access_for_stream with an info whose op is false returns the same result as check_ep0_access for the same (state, category) pair, regardless of whether requesting_stream is the designated root_client, is a different stream, or root_client is None

requirements.title: Root-client EP0 writes compose with the existing lifecycle-gated write check
requirements.text: check_ep0_access_for_stream with an info whose op is true, where requesting_stream equals root_client, returns the same result as check_ep0_access for the same (state, category) pair, for every RcServerState/RegisterCategory combination

requirements.title: Non-root EP0 writes are rejected with UnauthorizedAccess
requirements.text: check_ep0_access_for_stream with an info whose op is true returns Err(RcpError::UnauthorizedAccess) whenever requesting_stream does not equal root_client (including when root_client is None), for every RcServerState/RegisterCategory combination, without bypassing lifecycle-state gating when requesting_stream does equal root_client
requirements.tc18: §13.1 ("If within the RC Server's SERVER_config the ROOT_CLIENT is configured only the ROOT_CLIENT has write access to all RC Server configuration register maps. For other RC Clients than the ROOT_CLIENT write access is only given to EP_functional configuration of endpoints which are allocated to the RC Client within the EP_ID_config register map."), TC18.txt L3914-3916

requirements.title: Root-client-aware EP0 access check never panics
requirements.text: check_ep0_access_for_stream never panics for any RcServerState/RegisterCategory/op/requesting_stream/root_client combination

requirements.title: EndpointType numeric encoding and reserved-type flag
requirements.text: EndpointType enumerates the thirteen ep_type codes 0x01-0x0D named in ROADMAP.md Milestones 4 and 7, to_u8/from_u8 round-trip every defined code with no two codes colliding, and is_reserved returns true only for EndpointType::Dac
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: EndpointType::from_u8 rejects unrecognized bytes
requirements.text: EndpointType::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::Other) for every byte outside 0x01..=0x0D, without panicking
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: Three-layer taxonomy structural tagging
requirements.text: PerEpConfigBlock always belongs to ConfigLayer::Generic, CommonFunctionalConfig always belongs to ConfigLayer::CommonFunctional, and PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig::layer() reports ConfigLayer::PerTypeFunctional tagged with its own EndpointType, for every defined EndpointType

requirements.title: Cross-layer ep_type match invariant
requirements.text: functional_config_matches_ep_type returns true iff a PerEpConfigBlock and a PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig carry the same EndpointType, and check_functional_config_matches_ep_type returns Ok(()) in exactly that case and Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) otherwise, for every EndpointType pair

requirements.title: Provisional ConfigLayer to RegisterCategory mapping
requirements.text: register_category maps ConfigLayer::Generic to RegisterCategory::HwConfig, and both ConfigLayer::CommonFunctional and every ConfigLayer::PerTypeFunctional(EndpointType) variant to RegisterCategory::RcpConfig, agreeing with each other across every defined EndpointType

requirements.title: Register map taxonomy operations never panic
requirements.text: EndpointType::from_u8 never panics across the full 0..=255 byte range, and functional_config_matches_ep_type/check_functional_config_matches_ep_type/layer()/register_category never panic for any EndpointType pair

requirements.title: TableDescriptor encode/decode round-trip and short-input rejection
requirements.text: TableDescriptor::encode/decode round-trip every ptr/capacity pair exactly, decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN, and decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2900-3050

requirements.title: GeneralRegisters models the full §3.6 general register-map field set
requirements.text: GeneralRegisters carries the six ROADMAP.md-quoted fields (svr_oa_tc18_magic_nr, svr_version, svr_vendor_id, svr_device_id, svr_ep_count, svr_implemented_options) plus the remaining rows of this crate's own §3.6 table extraction, each independently settable/readable, defaults to an all-zero value, and reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::General
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2900-3050

requirements.title: GeneralRegisters encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: GeneralRegisters::encode/decode round-trip every field exactly (including all-default and all-max-value instances) via a fixed-length big-endian wire form, and decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2900-3050

requirements.title: GeneralRegisters::decode rejects short input
requirements.text: GeneralRegisters::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input strictly shorter than ENCODED_LEN, and succeeds for input of exactly ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2900-3050

requirements.title: GeneralRegisters/TableDescriptor encode/decode never panic
requirements.text: TableDescriptor::decode and GeneralRegisters::decode never panic for arbitrary byte slices of any length, and GeneralRegisters::encode/TableDescriptor::encode never panic for any field value
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2900-3050

requirements.title: HwPinMappingEntry models the §3.7 per-pin mapping row
requirements.text: HwPinMappingEntry carries hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, and an undecomposed hw_pin_props byte, and reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::HwConfig
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 ("HW_config"), TC18.txt L3088-3108

requirements.title: HwPinMappingEntry encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: HwPinMappingEntry::encode/decode round-trip every field exactly via a fixed-length big-endian wire form, and decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 ("HW_config"), TC18.txt L3088-3108

requirements.title: HwPinMappingEntry decode rejects short input and never panics
requirements.text: HwPinMappingEntry::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 ("HW_config"), TC18.txt L3088-3108

requirements.title: RequestStreamConfigEntry models TC18 Table 22's per-stream config row
requirements.text: RequestStreamConfigEntry carries the sixteen fields TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.7.7 Table 22 'Request stream configuration' (pp.57-58) tabulates — rx_stream_id (0x0000, 64 bit), rx_stream_max_request_size (0x0008, 16 bit), rx_wd_timeout_interval (0x000A, 16 bit), rx_secure_channel_index (0x000C, 8 bit), the eight 1-bit flags rx_enforce_e2e through rx_wd_info_enable sharing the bit-addressed byte 0x000D, rx_safestate_sequencer (0x000E), rx_safe_sequencer_state (0x000F), rx_ack_stream_index (0x0010), and rx_resp_stream_index (0x0011) — with the eight flags typed bool to match their 1-bit width, and reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::RcpConfig
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("Request stream configuration"), TC18.txt L3222-3293

requirements.title: RequestStreamConfigEntry encodes TC18 Table 22's 24-byte row layout
requirements.text: RequestStreamConfigEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 24, the row stride fixed by Table 22's own tabulation of the next row's rx_stream_id2 at relative address 0x0018. encode places every field at its tabulated relative address, packs the eight 1-bit flags into the single byte at FLAGS_OFFSET == 0x000D with rx_enforce_e2e at bit .0 through rx_wd_info_enable at bit .7 in the order Table 22 lists them, and writes the reserved 16-bit block at 0x0012 and reserved 32-bit block at 0x0014 as zero. encode/decode round-trip every specified field exactly (including all-default and all-flags-set instances) and decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("Request stream configuration"), TC18.txt L3222-3293

requirements.title: RequestStreamConfigEntry decode rejects short input, ignores reserved bytes, and never panics
requirements.text: RequestStreamConfigEntry::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN, ignores the content of TC18 Table 22's reserved bytes 0x0012-0x0017 entirely (so any reserved content decodes to the same value), and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("Request stream configuration"), TC18.txt L3222-3293

requirements.title: EpByteBusIdMapEntry models TC18 Table 23's EP_ID_config row and its end-of-table sentinel
requirements.text: EpByteBusIdMapEntry carries the three fields TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.7.8 Table 23 'EP_ID_config' (p.59) tabulates — map_stream_index (Request_Stream_Index, 0x0000, 8 bit), map_ep_nr (EP_Nr, 0x0001, 8 bit), and map_byte_bus_id (BBID, 0x0002, 16 bit carrying an 11-bit byte_bus_id) — reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::RcpConfig, and is_end_of_table returns true iff map_stream_index == END_OF_TABLE_STREAM_INDEX (0), per Table 23's note 'A Request_Stream_Index = 0 denotes the end of the table'. Per that same section, keeping rows in ascending order is the writing client's responsibility, so this module defines no ascending-order validation or enforcement
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8 Table 25 ("EP_ID_config (Request_stream & byte_bus_id mapping to Endpoints and their channels)"), TC18.txt L3327-3341

requirements.title: EpByteBusIdMapEntry encodes TC18 Table 23's 4-byte row layout
requirements.text: EpByteBusIdMapEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 4, the row stride fixed by Table 23's own tabulation of the next row's 2_Request_Stream_Index at relative address 0x0004. encode emits [Request_Stream_Index, EP_Nr, BBID big-endian] in that order — EP_Nr at 0x0001 precedes BBID at 0x0002 — and encode/decode round-trip every field exactly; decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8 Table 25 ("EP_ID_config (Request_stream & byte_bus_id mapping to Endpoints and their channels)"), TC18.txt L3327-3341

requirements.title: EpByteBusIdMapEntry decode rejects short input and never panics
requirements.text: EpByteBusIdMapEntry::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8 Table 25 ("EP_ID_config (Request_stream & byte_bus_id mapping to Endpoints and their channels)"), TC18.txt L3327-3341

requirements.title: ResponseStreamConfigEntry models the §3.10 response/ack queue config row
requirements.text: ResponseStreamConfigEntry carries resp_stream_uid, resp_max_avtpdu_size, resp_queue_size, resp_flush_on_count, and resp_flush_time, and reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::RcpConfig
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 Table 27 ("Responder QUEUE_config"), TC18.txt L3421-3444

requirements.title: ResponseStreamConfigEntry encode/decode round-trip
requirements.text: ResponseStreamConfigEntry::encode/decode round-trip every field exactly via a fixed-length big-endian wire form, and decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 Table 27 ("Responder QUEUE_config"), TC18.txt L3421-3444

requirements.title: ResponseStreamConfigEntry decode rejects short input and never panics
requirements.text: ResponseStreamConfigEntry::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 Table 27 ("Responder QUEUE_config"), TC18.txt L3421-3444

requirements.title: SequencerStateEntry models both TC18 Table 25 fields and the power-on default
requirements.text: SequencerStateEntry carries both fields TC18 v0.5.1_RC §12.7.10 Table 25 'SEQUENCER_config' (p.61) tabulates per sequencer — seq_state (0x0000, 8 bit) and request_stream_index (0x0001, 8 bit, 'refers the Client Nr allowed to access this sequencer', the access-control binding §12.7.10 describes as 'Each sequencer is dedicated to a specific RC Client and its bound endpoints') — giving a 2-byte row stride, fixed by Table 25's own tabulation of Seq_2's Seq_state at relative address 0x0002. It reports CATEGORY == lifecycle::RegisterCategory::RcpConfig, and power_on_default() returns seq_state == 1 per §12.7.10 ('Upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to "1"') with request_stream_index == 0, Table 25 documenting no default for that field
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28 ("SEQUENCER_config"), TC18.txt L3473-3493

requirements.title: SequencerStateEntry encodes TC18 Table 25's 2-byte row layout
requirements.text: SequencerStateEntry::ENCODED_LEN is 2 and encode emits [seq_state, request_stream_index] at Table 25's relative addresses 0x0000 and 0x0001, so that a multi-sequencer table decoded through decode_rows resolves Seq_2's Seq_state at offset 0x0002. encode/decode round-trip both fields exactly, and decode ignores any trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28 ("SEQUENCER_config"), TC18.txt L3473-3493

requirements.title: SequencerStateEntry decode rejects short input and never panics
requirements.text: SequencerStateEntry::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for every input shorter than ENCODED_LEN (2), including a 1-byte input, and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28 ("SEQUENCER_config"), TC18.txt L3473-3493

requirements.title: Generic config-table row encode_rows/decode_rows round-trip and never panic
requirements.text: encode_rows/decode_rows round-trip an arbitrary-length row slice for each of HwPinMappingEntry, RequestStreamConfigEntry, EpByteBusIdMapEntry, ResponseStreamConfigEntry, and SequencerStateEntry, decode_rows returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) when the input length is not an exact multiple of the row's ROW_LEN, and never panics for any input length

requirements.title: Discovery broadcast stream_id sentinel recognition
requirements.text: is_discovery_broadcast_stream_id returns true iff stream_id equals DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_STREAM_ID (sender_mac DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_SENDER_MAC paired with unique_id DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_UNIQUE_ID), and false for any other StreamId value including ones matching only the sender_mac or only the unique_id, without panicking
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 ("stream_id = streamMAC + unique_id ... unique_id = 0x0000"), TC18.txt L2750-2751

requirements.title: Discovery request construction and recognition
requirements.text: build_discovery_request produces an AcfAbbMessage addressed to EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID with op false (read direction) and a payload whose leading DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS_LEN bytes big-endian-decode to DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS (0), such that is_discovery_request(&result) is true, and the message round-trips through encode_acf_abb/decode_acf_abb unchanged with is_discovery_request still true afterward
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 Table 18 ("Discovery request"), TC18.txt L2746-2758

requirements.title: Discovery request recognition rejects non-matching shapes
requirements.text: is_discovery_request returns false when byte_bus_id is not EP0_BYTE_BUS_ID, when op is true (write direction), when the payload's leading DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS_LEN bytes decode to a register address other than 0, or when the payload is shorter than DISCOVERY_REGISTER_ADDRESS_LEN, and ignores any payload bytes beyond the register-address prefix
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 Table 18 ("Discovery request"), TC18.txt L2746-2758

requirements.title: Discovery response answerable in any lifecycle state
requirements.text: build_discovery_response succeeds for every RcServerState variant (HwUnconfigured, HwConfigured, RcpConfigured) by composing with lifecycle::check_register_reachable(state, RegisterCategory::General), producing a response whose byte_message_info echoes the request's byte_bus_id per the existing echo-back rule and whose payload equals general.encode() verbatim, round-tripping through encode_acf_abb/decode_acf_abb with GeneralRegisters::decode recovering the original content
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("An RC Server may receive a "discovery request" in any state of the life-cycle and shall send a "discovery response" in return"), TC18.txt L2731-2732

requirements.title: Discovery request/response helpers never panic
requirements.text: is_discovery_request never panics for any byte_bus_id/op/payload-length combination, build_discovery_response never panics for any RcServerState, and is_discovery_broadcast_stream_id never panics for any sampled sender_mac/unique_id combination

requirements.title: Discovery claim lapse boundary semantics
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim::has_lapsed returns false while elapsed time since claimed_at is strictly less than timeout, true once elapsed time reaches or exceeds timeout (inclusive boundary), and uses saturating_duration_since so that a now earlier than claimed_at reads as zero elapsed time rather than panicking or wrapping
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("If the RC Server does not receive configuration requests on the stream for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery"), TC18.txt L2733-2735

requirements.title: Discovery-stream first-claimant rule and Discovery_TimeOut lapse-and-reopen
requirements.text: try_claim_discovery_stream grants a claim timestamped now when current is None, grants and re-timestamps a claim when current already belongs to the same claimant (refresh), and grants a new claim to any claimant once the existing claim's has_lapsed is true as of now under timeout (Discovery_TimeOut lapse-and-reopen), with DISCOVERY_TIME_OUT defaulting to 20ms
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("The first discovery request the RC server receives in HW_UNCONFIGURED or HW_CONFIGURED state is used to set the discovery stream ... If the RC Server does not receive configuration requests on the stream for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery"), TC18.txt L2731-2735

requirements.title: Discovery-stream claim rejects a second live claimant
requirements.text: try_claim_discovery_stream returns Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when current holds a live (not lapsed) claim for a claimant different from the requested claimant, leaving the caller's own copy of the existing claim unaffected by the rejected attempt
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream. If others send configuration requests they will be rejected and get an error response"), TC18.txt L2735-2737

requirements.title: Discovery-stream claim rejects the broadcast sentinel as claimant
requirements.text: try_claim_discovery_stream returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) whenever the requested claimant equals DISCOVERY_BROADCAST_STREAM_ID, regardless of whether current is None, holds a live claim, or holds a lapsed claim

requirements.title: Discovery-stream claiming helpers never panic

requirements.title: Discovery cache staleness check has an inclusive boundary and never panics on out-of-order now

requirements.title: Discovery cache invalidate removes an entry and matches detects an identity change
requirements.text: DiscoveryCache::invalidate removes stream_id's cached entry if present (returning true) and is a no-op returning false if absent; DiscoveryCacheEntry::matches returns false when a freshly observed GeneralRegisters' cache-worthy subset differs from the entry's own, distinguishing a still-valid cache entry from a changed server identity at the same stream_id

requirements.title: Discovery cache operations never panic

requirements.title: UartRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 UART request after evt[2:0] validation, honestly split across UART's own independent TX/RX queues
requirements.text: UartRequest's three variants (Write(UartTxQueue), Read, ConfigWrite) give an incoming UART request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike I2cRequest/LinRequest/AdcRequest/PwmInRequest/CanRequest, each of which model one unified request shape for their endpoint type's single EP request storage, UartRequest's evt[2:0]==000b case splits into two structurally distinct variants (Write/Read) reflecting this module's own pre-existing UartTxQueue/UartRxQueue two-EP-request-storage split (TC18 13.7.8.1), which this crate confirms is a genuinely separate, orthogonal concern from evt[2:0] classification -- neither TC18 section cites the other. from_evt_sub_opcode therefore takes an explicit is_write: bool direction argument rather than guessing direction from the payload, reusing crate::acf::ByteMessageInfo::op's own true-is-write convention exactly as crate::authz::Policy's own is_write field already names it, rather than inventing a new UART-private direction type
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (UART is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.8.1/§13.7.8.3 UART EP request handling ("thus the UART EP has two EP request storages, one for transmitting data and one for receiving data" / "The byte_msg_payload in the request is the UART payload"), TC18.txt L5292-5293, L5392

requirements.title: UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Write/Read/ConfigWrite, rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, propagates validate_uart_read_request's own rejection on a non-empty Read payload, and follows I2C/LIN/ADC/PWM_IN's Ok(ConfigWrite) precedent rather than CAN's ConfigWriteNotImplemented departure, never panicking
requirements.text: UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode decodes a Plain (sub_opcode 0), is_write==true request's payload bytes as a UartTxQueue via UartTxQueue::decode (infallible), decodes a Plain, is_write==false request by re-enforcing validate_uart_read_request's own pre-existing payload-less-read-only rule and propagating its Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) unchanged for a non-empty payload, recognizes a ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request without attempting to interpret its payload or consult is_write (full TC18 12.7.1 config-write payload decoding is deferred, not silently guessed at), and returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) for every Reserved sub_opcode value, matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and every prior Row-2 endpoint-type module's identical refusal of its own table's reserved code. Unlike crate::can::CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode (which returns Err(RcpError::ConfigWriteNotImplemented) for evt[2:0]==111b because its own CanDataFrame-accepting signature cannot honestly construct a ConfigWrite variant from a caller-supplied value that is definitionally not a config-write payload), UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's ConfigWrite arm constructs no UART-specific value at all and so is under no such pressure -- it follows crate::i2c::I2cRequest's/crate::lin::LinRequest's/crate::adc::AdcRequest's/crate::pwm::PwmInRequest's original Ok(Self::ConfigWrite) precedent instead. Never panics for any sub_opcode/is_write/payload combination

requirements.text: PwmDurationPair's period and active_duration fields are independently settable u32 values, and PwmDurationPair::default() yields period == 0 and active_duration == 0
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 Figure 27 ("pwmo request format"), TC18.txt L5031-5038

requirements.title: AdcResolutionBits::new rejects zero and any bit width above 16, and never panics
requirements.text: AdcResolutionBits::new returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for 0 and for any value above 16, and never panics for any sampled u8 input
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 54 ("defines the number of bits to be used of the ADC reading value (<=16)"), TC18.txt L5529-5531

requirements.title: PwmOutFunctionalConfig defaults to a zeroed target PwmDurationPair
requirements.text: PwmOutFunctionalConfig::default().target equals PwmDurationPair::default()
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("To stop PWM signal generation a request with PWM_Period of '0' shall be issued."), TC18.txt L5050-5052

requirements.title: AdcResolutionBits::max_raw_value computes 2^bits - 1, and default() resolves to 16 bits
requirements.text: AdcResolutionBits::max_raw_value returns 2^bits - 1 for every valid bit width including the u16::MAX boundary at 16 bits, and AdcResolutionBits::default resolves to the widest modeled resolution, 16 bits, as this crate's own unconfirmed-default placeholder
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 54 ("defines the number of bits to be used of the ADC reading value (<=16)"), TC18.txt L5529-5531

requirements.title: PwmOutFunctionalConfig::layer_tag matches EndpointType::PwmOut and rejects EndpointType::PwmIn
requirements.text: PwmOutFunctionalConfig::layer_tag returns a PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::PwmOut that satisfies regmap::functional_config_matches_ep_type/check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a PerEpConfigBlock also tagged EndpointType::PwmOut, and does not satisfy it against a PerEpConfigBlock tagged EndpointType::PwmIn

requirements.title: AdcSampleValue round-trips through encode/decode within its resolution and rejects raw values wider than that resolution, and never panics
requirements.text: AdcSampleValue::new/AdcSampleValue::decode/AdcSampleValue::encode round-trip any raw value within AdcResolutionBits::max_raw_value as a 2-byte big-endian wire form, reject any raw value exceeding that maximum with RcpError::InvalidParameter, and decode never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.2 Table 54 ("defines the number of bits to be used of the ADC reading value (<=16)"), TC18.txt L5529-5531

requirements.title: PwmInFunctionalConfig defaults to a zero no_signal_timeout
requirements.text: PwmInFunctionalConfig::default().no_signal_timeout equals 0
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.2 Table 48 ("pwmi functional configuration"), TC18.txt L5104-5149

requirements.title: AdcFunctionalConfig defaults to the default AdcResolutionBits and a zeroed AdcAveragingConfig
requirements.text: AdcFunctionalConfig::default carries AdcResolutionBits::default (16 bits) and a zero-valued AdcAveragingConfig (adc_sample_interval, adc_avg_intervals_per_request, and adc_combine_avg_values all zero)

requirements.title: PwmInFunctionalConfig::layer_tag matches EndpointType::PwmIn and rejects EndpointType::PwmOut
requirements.text: PwmInFunctionalConfig::layer_tag returns a PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::PwmIn that satisfies regmap::functional_config_matches_ep_type/check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a PerEpConfigBlock also tagged EndpointType::PwmIn, and does not satisfy it against a PerEpConfigBlock tagged EndpointType::PwmOut

requirements.title: AdcFunctionalConfig's layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Adc cross-layer rule
requirements.text: AdcFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Adc that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: resolve_pwm_in_read reports Measured(pair) whenever elapsed_since_last_edge is below no_signal_timeout and a measurement exists
requirements.text: resolve_pwm_in_read returns Some(PwmInReadResolution::Measured(pair)) whenever last_measured is Some(pair) and elapsed_since_last_edge is strictly less than config.no_signal_timeout
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.3 ("The PWM_IN request and response contain two 16 bit values in the payload. Responses include the measured active time of the PWM signal as well as the period"), TC18.txt L5169-5170

requirements.title: resolve_adc_sample_window_ticks chains adc_sample_interval, adc_avg_intervals_per_request, and adc_combine_avg_values into a total elapsed tick count, and never panics
requirements.text: resolve_adc_sample_window_ticks multiplies adc_avg_intervals_per_request by adc_combine_avg_values by adc_sample_interval to produce the total elapsed tick count one combined result takes to produce, using checked (never-wrapping, never-panicking) arithmetic throughout including at the all-MAX field-width boundary, and never panics for any sampled AdcAveragingConfig
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("further samples are taken with a timely distance of one 'adc_sample_interval'"), TC18.txt L5452-5453

requirements.title: resolve_pwm_in_read reports NoSignal once the timeout elapses, never re-reporting a stale prior measurement
requirements.text: resolve_pwm_in_read returns Some(PwmInReadResolution::NoSignal) whenever elapsed_since_last_edge is greater than or equal to config.no_signal_timeout, regardless of whether last_measured carries a prior value, and a zero-valued no_signal_timeout is not treated as a disabled sentinel
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.2 Table 48 ("0b: if MAX PERIOD is exceeded, invalidate measurement and wait for new active phase of signal"), TC18.txt L5129-5135

requirements.title: resolve_adc_averaged_value computes the two-level averaging pipeline over raw samples
requirements.text: resolve_adc_averaged_value groups raw_samples into adc_avg_intervals_per_request-sized groups, averages each group (level one), then averages the first adc_combine_avg_values group averages into the returned combined result (level two), ignoring any trailing raw samples beyond what the pipeline consumes
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("the average is calculated. Finally, the COMBINE_NR_VAL defines how many measurement values (i.e. averaging results) will be put in one response frame"), TC18.txt L5455-5457

requirements.title: resolve_pwm_in_read returns None while genuinely awaiting a first edge before the timeout elapses, rather than hanging
requirements.text: resolve_pwm_in_read returns None when last_measured is None and elapsed_since_last_edge is strictly less than config.no_signal_timeout, letting a polling caller retry instead of this function blocking
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.2 Table 48 ("0b: pwmi measures once after request received (a response is delayed until the next measurement is finalized)"), TC18.txt L5136-5142

requirements.title: resolve_adc_averaged_value rejects a malformed averaging pipeline configuration, and never panics
requirements.text: resolve_adc_averaged_value returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when adc_avg_intervals_per_request or adc_combine_avg_values is zero, when raw_samples carries fewer raw samples than the pipeline requires (including at the u16::MAX/u16::MAX field-width boundary), or defensively if their product would overflow usize, and never panics for any sampled AdcAveragingConfig/raw_samples combination

requirements.title: validate_adc_sample_request accepts AdcSamplingMode::RequestDriven and rejects AdcSamplingMode::Continuous with RcpError::UnsupportedCmd
requirements.text: validate_adc_sample_request returns Ok(()) for AdcSamplingMode::RequestDriven (also AdcSamplingMode's default) and Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) for AdcSamplingMode::Continuous, enforcing the roadmap's request-driven-sampling-only rule since no free-running/continuous sampling mode is permitted
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("The ADC only samples the input, when a request is executed. Consequently, no trigger will occur when there is no request to sample"), TC18.txt L5476-5477

requirements.title: AdcRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 ADC request after evt[2:0] validation
requirements.text: AdcRequest's two variants (Plain, ConfigWrite) give an incoming ADC request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike I2cRequest::Plain, AdcRequest::Plain carries no decoded payload struct at all, since TC18 §13.7.9.3 states the ADC request itself carries no byte_msg_payload
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (ADC is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.9.3 ADC request handling, TC18.txt L5577-5579

requirements.title: AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain/ConfigWrite, rejects a non-empty Plain payload with InvalidParameter and Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, never panicking
requirements.text: AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode recognizes a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request only when payload is empty, per TC18 §13.7.9.3's statement that the ADC request has no byte_msg_payload -- a non-empty payload on a Plain request returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter), this crate's general malformed-input sentinel, since TC18 names no dedicated violation code for this specific case (distinct from Table 33's own Reserved sub_opcode rule, which does name UNSUPPORTED_CMD). A ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request is recognized without attempting to interpret its payload (full TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload decoding is deferred, not silently guessed at). Every Reserved sub_opcode value returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and crate::i2c::I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's identical refusal of its own table's reserved code; never panics for any sub_opcode/payload combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.9.3 ("The ADC request has no byte_msg_payload, while a wait-request needs a byte_msg_payload"), TC18.txt L5577-5579

requirements.title: resolve_pwm_in_read never panics for any sampled combination of config, last_measured, and elapsed inputs
requirements.text: resolve_pwm_in_read does not panic across sampled boundary combinations of no_signal_timeout (including 0 and u32::MAX), last_measured (None, a zeroed pair, and a maximal pair), and elapsed_since_last_edge (including 0 and u32::MAX)
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.2 Table 48 ("pwmi functional configuration"), TC18.txt L5104-5149

requirements.title: EvtGroup's three roadmap-named group labels round-trip through an ordinal encoding
requirements.text: EvtGroup::to_u8/from_u8 round-trip every one of the three roadmap-listed group labels (A, B, C) with ordinal values 0, 1, 2 respectively, giving the still-unclassified group letters a concrete, testable type per Guiding Principle 5

requirements.title: EvtGroup::from_u8 rejects every ordinal value outside 0..=2
requirements.text: EvtGroup::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for every raw value outside 0..=2 and never panics for any input

requirements.title: classify_evt_sub_opcode returns Ok(None) for every in-range sub_opcode value
requirements.text: classify_evt_sub_opcode returns Ok(None) for every sub_opcode value in 0..=EVT_SUB_OPCODE_MAX, honestly reporting that no Groups A/B/C classification is confirmed for any evt.sub_opcode value rather than guessing one, per Guiding Principle 5

requirements.title: classify_evt_sub_opcode rejects out-of-range sub_opcode values and never panics
requirements.text: classify_evt_sub_opcode returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for every sub_opcode value greater than EVT_SUB_OPCODE_MAX, and never panics for any u8 input across the full 0..=255 range

requirements.title: EvtRow2Kind enumerates TC18 Table 33's three Row-2 evt[2:0] outcomes
requirements.text: EvtRow2Kind's three variants (Plain, Reserved, ConfigWrite) give TC18 Table 33's Row-2 endpoint-type group ({ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO}) evt[2:0] rule an explicit, round-trippable classification shape, shared across every Row-2 endpoint-type module rather than re-derived per type
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row ({ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO}), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: evt_row2_kind_of classifies sub_opcode values 1-6 and every value above 7 as Reserved, and never panics
requirements.text: evt_row2_kind_of returns EvtRow2Kind::Reserved for every sub_opcode value in 1..=6 (matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 reserved range, which both this crate's resolution and the table's own literal cell text agree on) and for every value above 7 (sub_opcode's u8 type does not itself enforce the 3-bit field width), and never panics for any u8 input across the full 0..=255 range
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085

requirements.title: evt_row2_kind_of resolves evt[2:0]=000b as Plain and 111b as ConfigWrite, reconciling Table 33's literal Row-2 cell text
requirements.text: evt_row2_kind_of returns EvtRow2Kind::Plain for sub_opcode 0 and EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite for sub_opcode 7.
