The Plain classification for 0 does NOT follow TC18 Table 33's own printed Row-2 cell text literally ("000b to 110b reserved", which includes 000b) -- this crate resolves that literal text as a drafting defect and instead follows TC18 §12.9.1's general "evt[2:0] != 0" rule (implying 0 is every endpoint type's normal case), §13.7.7.3's own I2C request-handling description (which names no reserved evt[2:0] value), and the cross-repo resolution this crate's sibling c-RCP centralizes as rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain(), recorded in RELAY's docs/RCP-ARCHITECTURE.md. This entry is deliberately left without a tc18_master_id: docs/tc18-master-catalog.json's own TC18-13.5-001 summary states the literal (000b-included) reading, which is the exact fact this requirement's Plain-for-0 claim does NOT implement
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 cell (TC18.txt L4085, literal text: "000b to 110b reserved") reconciled against §12.9.1 (TC18.txt L3611, "If evt[2:0] ≠ 0 and no byte_msg_payload is present, then an error response shall be sent with the error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD") and §13.7.7.3's I2C request-handling description (TC18.txt L5240-5242)

requirements.title: CommonFunctionalConfig models ep_enable/ep_clear_req_storage/ep_req_crc_enable and encodes each as a full byte
requirements.text: CommonFunctionalConfig carries the three roadmap-named common functional-config fields (ep_enable, ep_clear_req_storage, ep_req_crc_enable) as bool fields, defaults to all-false, and CommonFunctionalConfig::encode produces a fixed 3-byte [0x00/0x01, 0x00/0x01, 0x00/0x01] wire form with no panics for any field combination
requirements.tc18: §13.7 Table 35 ("EP functional config common entries"), TC18.txt L4298-4343

requirements.title: CommonFunctionalConfig::decode round-trips encode's output and rejects short input
requirements.text: CommonFunctionalConfig::decode(encode(cfg)) == Ok(cfg) for every sampled field combination, decode treats any nonzero byte as true, decode ignores trailing bytes beyond ENCODED_LEN, and decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for any input shorter than CommonFunctionalConfig::ENCODED_LEN
requirements.tc18: §13.7 Table 35 ("EP functional config common entries"), TC18.txt L4298-4343

requirements.title: RequestKind models compound (0x0F) and compound-wait (0x0B) discriminants and round-trips to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind carries the two roadmap-named conditional-request discriminants (Compound = 0x0F, CompoundWait = 0x0B) and RequestKind::to_u8/from_u8 round-trip both values
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("Different types of conditional requests"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: RequestKind::from_u8 rejects every discriminant value other than the two named ones and never panics
requirements.text: RequestKind::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte other than 0x0B/0x0F, including the other conditional-request kinds ROADMAP.md names elsewhere in Milestone 5 that this module does not yet model, and never panics across the full 0..=255 byte range

requirements.title: SequencerState and CompoundGateConfig model a sequencer number and its required start state
requirements.text: SequencerState wraps a single persistent-state byte mirroring regmap::SequencerStateEntry::seq_state, and CompoundGateConfig pairs a plain sequencer_num byte with the SequencerState a compound/compound-wait request requires before it may execute; both default to zero
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("Usage of GBB message for compound requests"), TC18.txt L1434-1438 (field rows); Table 7's own caption now sits at L1458, ~20-24 lines later after a TC18.txt re-extraction shifted it

requirements.title: check_sequencer_num_in_bounds validates a sequencer number against svr_sequencers_max
requirements.text: check_sequencer_num_in_bounds returns Ok(()) for every sequencer_num strictly less than svr_sequencers_max and Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) otherwise (including when svr_sequencers_max is 0), and never panics for any sampled input; check_compound_gate applies this bounds check ahead of its own state comparison
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("An RC Server implementation may support only a lower number of sequencers."), TC18.txt L3870-3871

requirements.title: is_gate_satisfied/check_compound_gate implement the sequencer-gated execution rule
requirements.text: is_gate_satisfied returns true only when the supplied current sequencer state equals the gate's configured start_state; check_compound_gate returns Ok(()) when the sequencer is known and its state satisfies the gate, and Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when the sequencer is known but its state does not satisfy the gate; neither ever panics
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("cmp_start_state Defines the state the addressed sequencer has to reach to start this request"), TC18.txt L1434-1435

requirements.title: CompoundExecDelays models cmp_exec_delay/cmpw_exec_delay and resolve_compound_exec_delay selects the matching timer
requirements.text: CompoundExecDelays carries cmp_exec_delay and cmpw_exec_delay as independent u32 fields defaulting to zero, and resolve_compound_exec_delay returns Some(cmp_exec_delay) for RequestKind::Compound, Some(cmpw_exec_delay) for RequestKind::CompoundWait, and None for RequestKind::Triggered (which has no CompoundExecDelays field of its own)
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("cmp_exec_delay delay time between the sequencer reaching the state defined in start_state and the start of the execution of the request"), TC18.txt L1439-1442

requirements.title: advance_sequencer_if_still_in_start_state implements the advance-only-if-still-in-start-state race guard
requirements.text: advance_sequencer_if_still_in_start_state returns Some(next_state) only when the observed sequencer state at advance time still equals the gate's start_state, and returns None (do not advance) when a race has moved the sequencer out of its start state in the interim; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("In RF state the state of sequencer cmp_sequencer is set to cmp_next_state if the sequencer state still equals the cmp_start_state, else the sequencer state is not changed."), TC18.txt L3698-3705

requirements.title: RequestKind binds to the leading byte of AcfGbbMessage::message_timestamp for GBB conditional requests
requirements.text: RequestKind::from_gbb_message_timestamp extracts the leading (most significant) byte of an already-decoded AcfGbbMessage::message_timestamp value and decodes it via RequestKind::from_u8, returning Some(kind) for any of the eleven non-Standard discriminants and None for a leading byte of 0x00 or any other unrecognized byte -- never Standard, since 0x00 at this wire position cannot be distinguished from a genuine unconditional request's ordinary timestamp data. RequestKind::to_gbb_message_timestamp is the companion encode-side helper: it writes self's discriminant into the leading byte of a caller-supplied message_timestamp while preserving the low 56 bits unchanged, and returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for RequestKind::Standard rather than injecting its unconfirmed 0x00 placeholder. Both are internally consistent with encode_acf_gbb/decode_acf_gbb's existing big-endian to_be_bytes()/from_be_bytes() layout of message_timestamp, and neither ever panics for any input.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("The first byte in the message_timestamp field is used to indicate the type of condition."), TC18.txt L1254-1259

requirements.title: RequestKind gains a Triggered = 0x0E variant that round-trips through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind::Triggered encodes to discriminant byte 0x0E via to_u8, RequestKind::from_u8(0x0E) decodes to RequestKind::Triggered, and every RequestKind variant (Compound, CompoundWait, Triggered) round-trips through to_u8/from_u8; from_u8 continues to reject every other byte value and never panics across the full 0..=255 range
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("Different types of conditional requests"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: TriggerExecDelay models trigger_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay selects it only for RequestKind::Triggered
requirements.text: TriggerExecDelay carries trigger_exec_delay as a single u32 field defaulting to zero, and resolve_trigger_exec_delay returns Some(delay.0) for RequestKind::Triggered and None for every other RequestKind
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_exec_delay In multiples of ep_delay_time ... for the request execution after the trigger occurred the as many times as specified by trigger_threshold"), TC18.txt L1719-1723

requirements.title: TriggerRepeatCount models a Triggered request's occurrence repeat count with an explicit infinite-repeat sentinel
requirements.text: TriggerRepeatCount::from_u16 decodes raw value 0xFFFF (TRIGGER_REPEAT_COUNT_INFINITE_SENTINEL) to TriggerRepeatCount::Infinite and every other raw u16 value to TriggerRepeatCount::Finite(raw); TriggerRepeatCount::to_u16 encodes Finite(n) back to n and Infinite back to 0xFFFF; every value produced by from_u16 round-trips through to_u16/from_u16, while a directly-constructed Finite(0xFFFF) deliberately collapses to Infinite on the next from_u16 decode since the wire has only the one sentinel value
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_repetitions ... If set to 0xFFFF it indicates infinite repetition and no decrease is done at end of execution."), TC18.txt L1724-1728

requirements.title: is_trigger_repeat_exhausted determines whether a Triggered request's occurrence count has been exhausted
requirements.text: is_trigger_repeat_exhausted returns false for every occurrences_so_far value when repeat_count is TriggerRepeatCount::Infinite (it never exhausts on its own), and returns true once occurrences_so_far is greater than or equal to the finite configured target; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_repetitions ... If the field has a zero at the end of the execution, the request will be removed from the EP request storage, otherwise decreased by one."), TC18.txt L1724-1728

requirements.title: should_count_trigger_occurrence counts only the trigger the request selected, independent of endpoint busy/idle state
requirements.text: should_count_trigger_occurrence(step, source_ep, signal_nr) shall return true iff source_ep == step.trigger_source_ep and signal_nr == step.trigger_signal_nr; it takes no busy/idle input, so occurrence counting is independent of the target endpoint's idle state (c-RCP request.h:291-303, rcp_triggered_runtime_record_occurrence()).
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 ("for trigger requests the fulfillment of the trigger condition and start of the trigger delay time shall be independent of the idle state of the endpoint."), TC18.txt L3743-3744

requirements.title: RequestKind gains a Chained = 0x01 variant that round-trips through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind::Chained encodes to discriminant byte 0x01 via to_u8, RequestKind::from_u8(0x01) decodes to RequestKind::Chained, and every RequestKind variant (Chained, CompoundWait, Triggered, Compound) round-trips through to_u8/from_u8; resolve_compound_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay both return None for RequestKind::Chained to stay exhaustive over the now four-variant RequestKind; from_u8 continues to reject every other byte value and never panics across the full 0..=255 range
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("Different types of conditional requests"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: check_chain_continuation implements the cs-bit abort-on-predecessor-error rule for chained requests
requirements.text: check_chain_continuation returns Err(RcpError::ChainAborted) when cs is true and predecessor_errored is true, and Ok(()) in every other combination (cs false regardless of predecessor_errored, or predecessor_errored false regardless of cs); never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 Table 11 ("cs Conditional start ... 1b: request will not be executed in case the previous request returned an error ... error response with error code = CHAIN_ABORTED."), TC18.txt L1833-1837

requirements.title: RcpError gains ChainAborted and ChainError as two new, distinct variants for the chained-request error codes
requirements.text: RcpError::ChainAborted and RcpError::ChainError are added as two new variants (not collapsed onto RequestRejected or any other of the eleven Milestone 2 TC18 error codes), are distinct from each other under equality, and their Display text embeds the roadmap-named CHAIN_ABORTED/CHAIN_ERROR codes respectively, following the enum's established "rcp/error: <CODE> - ..." message convention
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 Table 30 ("Error codes in responses"), TC18.txt L3839-3844

requirements.title: RequestKind gains a Timed = 0x0A variant that round-trips through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind::Timed encodes to discriminant byte 0x0A via to_u8, RequestKind::from_u8(0x0A) decodes to RequestKind::Timed, and every RequestKind variant (Chained, Timed, CompoundWait, Triggered, Compound) round-trips through to_u8/from_u8; resolve_compound_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay both return None for RequestKind::Timed to stay exhaustive over the now five-variant RequestKind; from_u8 continues to reject every other byte value and never panics across the full 0..=255 range
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("Different types of conditional requests"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: TimedExecutionTime models a Timed request's 48-bit presentation_time
requirements.text: TimedExecutionTime wraps a 48-bit presentation_time (request::TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX = 2^48-1, modulus 2^48, TC18 §11.2.2.7 Table 12 "(AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^48"), as c-RCP's timed request does (c-RCP/include/rcp/request.h:1017-1024); TimedExecutionTime::new rejects a value above TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX with InvalidSize (never silently truncated); there is no untimed sentinel and 0 is an ordinary presentation time.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Table 12 ("Usage of GBB message for timed request": presentation_time = (AS_sec × 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^48)

requirements.title: is_timed_request_ready / timed_due implement the presentation-time readiness rule
requirements.text: request::timed_due(presentation_time, now) returns true iff the forward delta (presentation_time - now) mod 2^48 is 0 or exceeds 2^47, bit-for-bit as c-RCP rcp_timed_due() (c-RCP/src/request.c:844-869); is_timed_request_ready(now, exec_time) equals timed_due(exec_time.presentation_time(), now), correctly handling the 48-bit rollover; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("In any case the presentation_time is the earliest point in time, when the request shall be executed."), TC18.txt L1951-1952

requirements.title: RequestKind gains ClearAll = 0x05, ClearNonSafestate = 0x06, and ClearSingle = 0x07 variants that round-trip through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind::ClearAll/ClearNonSafestate/ClearSingle encode to discriminant bytes 0x05/0x06/0x07 respectively via to_u8, RequestKind::from_u8 decodes each byte back to the matching variant, and every RequestKind variant (Chained, ClearAll, ClearNonSafestate, ClearSingle, Timed, CompoundWait, Triggered, Compound) round-trips through to_u8/from_u8; resolve_compound_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay both return None for all three cancellation variants to stay exhaustive over the now eight-variant RequestKind; from_u8 continues to reject every other byte value and never panics across the full 0..=255 range

requirements.title: check_clear_all_cancellation implements the clear-all (0x05, mandatory) cancellation rule
requirements.text: check_clear_all_cancellation always returns Err(RcpError::RequestCanceled), the uniform per-request outcome for a mandatory clear-all cancellation that cancels every pending/in-flight request it is applied to; never panics
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 ("Clear all requests (mandatory) ... the request type (first byte in the message_timestamp field) is 0x05."), TC18.txt L1983-1985

requirements.title: check_clear_non_safestate_cancellation implements the clear-non-safestate (0x06, optional) cancellation rule
requirements.text: check_clear_non_safestate_cancellation(is_safestate_related) returns Ok(()) (do not cancel) when is_safestate_related is true, and Err(RcpError::RequestCanceled) when is_safestate_related is false, capturing the rule that clear-non-safestate cancels every pending/in-flight request except one actively driving an endpoint toward its configured safe state; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 ("Clear all non-safestate requests (optional feature) ... the request type ... is 0x06."), TC18.txt L2054-2056

requirements.title: ClearTransactionNum and check_clear_single_cancellation implement the clear-single (0x07, optional) cancellation rule
requirements.text: ClearTransactionNum wraps a u8 matching acf::ByteMessageInfo::transaction_num's own width, defaulting to zero; check_clear_single_cancellation(candidate_transaction_num, target) returns Err(RcpError::RequestCanceled) when candidate_transaction_num equals target.0, and Ok(()) (do not cancel) for every other candidate value, capturing the rule that clear-single cancels exactly one pending request identified by clear_transaction_num; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("Clear one single request (optional feature) ... the request type ... is 0x07 followed by the transaction_num of the request to be cancelled."), TC18.txt L2140-2144

requirements.title: SequencerBank::new builds a persistent sequencer-state bank bounded by svr_sequencers_max, defaulting to power-on state 1
requirements.text: SequencerBank::new(svr_sequencers_max) allocates one SequencerState per sequencer number, sized to svr_sequencers_max (0 yielding an empty bank, mirroring check_sequencer_num_in_bounds's own 'no sequencers exist' reading), with every sequencer initialized to regmap::SequencerStateEntry::power_on_default's already-confirmed state 1 rather than re-deriving that value; SequencerBank::svr_sequencers_max() reports the bound the bank was constructed with; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("After power-on/reset all sequencers are in state 1."), TC18.txt L3866

requirements.title: SequencerBank::read returns a sequencer's live persistent state or SequencerNotKnown for an out-of-bounds sequencer number
requirements.text: SequencerBank::read(sequencer_num) returns Ok(SequencerState) for any sequencer_num within this bank's svr_sequencers_max bound, reusing check_sequencer_num_in_bounds's existing bound check, and Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for any sequencer_num at or beyond that bound, including against a bank constructed with svr_sequencers_max of 0; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.10 ("An RC Server implementation may support only a lower number of sequencers."), TC18.txt L3870-3871

requirements.title: SequencerBank::advance_if_still_in_start_state composes the advance-only-if-still-in-start-state race guard against this bank's own live, mutable store
requirements.text: SequencerBank::advance_if_still_in_start_state(gate, next_state) returns Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for an out-of-bounds gate.sequencer_num; otherwise it reads this bank's own stored state for gate.sequencer_num and delegates to advance_sequencer_if_still_in_start_state, returning Ok(true) and updating the stored state to next_state when the sequencer was still in gate.start_state, or Ok(false) with the store left unchanged when a race moved it out of that state first; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("In RF state the state of sequencer cmp_sequencer is set to cmp_next_state if the sequencer state still equals the cmp_start_state, else the sequencer state is not changed."), TC18.txt L3698-3705

requirements.title: SequencerBank::check_compound_gate composes SequencerBank::read with the free-function check_compound_gate against this bank's own live state
requirements.text: SequencerBank::check_compound_gate(gate) reads gate.sequencer_num's current state from this bank via SequencerBank::read and passes it to the free-function check_compound_gate together with this bank's own svr_sequencers_max, returning Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for an out-of-bounds sequencer, Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when the sequencer is known but not in gate.start_state, and Ok(()) when the gate is satisfied, giving check_compound_gate a genuine backing store instead of a caller-supplied current_state; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("cmp_start_state Defines the state the addressed sequencer has to reach to start this request"), TC18.txt L1434-1435

requirements.title: RequestKind gains a ninth Standard variant, with its own crate-local (spec-unconfirmed) 0x00 discriminant, round-tripping through to_u8/from_u8
requirements.text: RequestKind::Standard models the unconditional request kind ROADMAP.md's execution-priority ordering names as its lowest tier; to_u8()/from_u8() round-trip RequestKind::Standard through the crate-local placeholder discriminant 0x00, which is not a transcription of any confirmed OPEN Alliance TC18 wire value (see src/request.rs's own 'Provenance note: RequestKind::Standard's discriminant'); never panics for any input

requirements.title: resolve_compound_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay both widen to stay exhaustive over RequestKind::Standard, returning None
requirements.text: resolve_compound_exec_delay(RequestKind::Standard, _) and resolve_trigger_exec_delay(RequestKind::Standard, _) both return None, since RequestKind::Standard has no cmp_exec_delay/cmpw_exec_delay/trigger_exec_delay timer of its own, matching the None precedent already set for every other non-owning RequestKind variant; never panics for any input

requirements.title: ExecutionPriorityTier/execution_priority_tier collapse RequestKind's nine values down to the roadmap's seven named priority tiers, in the stated order
requirements.text: execution_priority_tier(kind) maps every RequestKind value to one of seven ExecutionPriorityTier variants ordered cancellation > triggered > timed > compound > compound-wait > chained > standard, the exact order ROADMAP.md's 'Execution priority ordering' checklist bullet states; RequestKind::ClearAll, RequestKind::ClearNonSafestate, and RequestKind::ClearSingle all collapse onto the single ExecutionPriorityTier::Cancellation tier; ExecutionPriorityTier's derived Ord orders a higher-priority tier as strictly less than every lower-priority tier; never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3652-3659

requirements.title: select_next_pending_request selects the highest-priority-tier pending request, breaking same-tier ties by earliest arrival_seq (FIFO)
requirements.text: select_next_pending_request(pending) returns None for an empty slice, and otherwise returns the index of the PendingRequestKey entry whose execution_priority_tier is highest priority, breaking ties among same-tier entries by the lowest (earliest) arrival_seq -- the checklist's own 'FIFO within a tier' rule; arrival_seq is a caller-supplied, presumed-monotonically-increasing marker rather than a value this crate reads from an owned queue, since no unified pending-request queue type exists yet; never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("When two or more requests with the same priority are due then starting the execution shall happen in the order with which the requests arrived in the EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3663-3664

requirements.title: RequestLifecycleState and is_request_lifecycle_transition_defined model the four-state pending/started/under-execution/finalized lifecycle and its three linear forward hops only
requirements.text: RequestLifecycleState has exactly four variants (Pending, Started, UnderExecution, Finalized) in that order, carrying no numeric encoding; is_request_lifecycle_transition_defined(from, to) is true only for (Pending, Started), (Started, UnderExecution), and (UnderExecution, Finalized), and false for every other (from, to) pair among the four states, including identity, backward, and skip transitions; never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 ("Once a request has been filed into an EP request storage, it is in the state 'request pending' ... enters the state 'request started' (RS) ... advances to 'request under execution' (RE) ... and then to 'request finalized' (RF)"), TC18.txt L3677-3682

requirements.title: RequestLifecycleState::try_transition rejects every undefined transition shape before consulting any type-specific guard
requirements.text: RequestLifecycleState::try_transition(self, target, input) returns Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) for any (self, target) pair is_request_lifecycle_transition_defined does not name, regardless of input; for a defined pair it delegates to the type-specific guard and returns Ok(target) on success or that guard's own Err otherwise; self-consuming (takes self by value, does not mutate anything in place); never panics for any sampled state pair or RequestLifecycleGuardInput value

requirements.title: The Pending -> Started hop composes check_compound_gate for Compound/CompoundWait and is_timed_request_ready for Timed, and passes unconditionally for every other RequestKind
requirements.text: RequestLifecycleState::Pending.try_transition(RequestLifecycleState::Started, input) composes check_compound_gate for RequestLifecycleGuardInput::Compound/CompoundWait (propagating Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for an out-of-bounds sequencer or Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) for a known-but-unsatisfied gate), composes is_timed_request_ready for RequestLifecycleGuardInput::Timed (Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when not yet ready, Ok(Started) once ready), and returns Ok(Started) unconditionally for Standard/Chained/ClearAll/ClearNonSafestate/ClearSingle/Triggered inputs; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("Execution procedure"), TC18.txt L3687-3739

requirements.title: The Started -> UnderExecution hop composes check_chain_continuation for Chained and the triggered fire predicate for Triggered, and passes unconditionally for every other RequestKind
requirements.text: RequestLifecycleState::Started.try_transition(RequestLifecycleState::UnderExecution, input) composes check_chain_continuation for RequestLifecycleGuardInput::Chained (propagating Err(RcpError::ChainAborted) when cs is set and the predecessor errored, Ok(UnderExecution) otherwise), composes TriggeredRuntime::fire_ready for RequestLifecycleGuardInput::Triggered (Ok(UnderExecution) iff the runtime is started, its threshold is reached, trigger_exec_delay has elapsed and the endpoint is idle, Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) otherwise -- c-RCP rcp_triggered_tick()), and returns Ok(UnderExecution) unconditionally for Standard/ClearAll/ClearNonSafestate/ClearSingle/Timed/Compound/CompoundWait inputs; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("Execution procedure"), TC18.txt L3687-3739

requirements.title: The UnderExecution -> Finalized hop is unconditional for every RequestKind
requirements.text: RequestLifecycleState::UnderExecution.try_transition(RequestLifecycleState::Finalized, input) returns Ok(RequestLifecycleState::Finalized) for every RequestLifecycleGuardInput variant sampled across all nine RequestKind values, since no checklist-named rule gates completion separately from the eligibility/continuation gates already applied at the two earlier hops; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("Execution procedure"), TC18.txt L3687-3739

requirements.title: try_force_cancel_all/try_force_cancel_non_safestate/try_force_cancel_single force a target request straight to Finalized per the cancellation trio's own check_clear_*_cancellation rule, idempotently
requirements.text: try_force_cancel_all(current) always sets *current to RequestLifecycleState::Finalized and returns Err(RcpError::RequestCanceled) unless *current is already Finalized, in which case it is left unchanged and Ok(()) is returned; try_force_cancel_non_safestate(current, is_safestate_related) and try_force_cancel_single(current, candidate_transaction_num, target) apply the same Finalized-forcing/idempotent shape, delegating to check_clear_non_safestate_cancellation and check_clear_single_cancellation respectively to decide whether *current is force-canceled; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1976-1978

requirements.title: GeneralRegisters::claims_compound_wait_bundle reads svr_implemented_options bit 0, this crate's placeholder position for the compound&wait option bundle
requirements.text: GeneralRegisters::claims_compound_wait_bundle(&self) returns true only when bit 0 of svr_implemented_options is set, and false otherwise, regardless of the state of any other bit in the bitmask; never panics for any sampled svr_implemented_options value
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 ("a: compound & wait requests"), TC18.txt L2935-2941

requirements.title: check_ep_type_supported gives EndpointType::is_reserved a structural consequence, closing ROADMAP.md Milestone 7's DAC decision
requirements.text: check_ep_type_supported(ep_type) returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd) for every EndpointType with is_reserved() true (EndpointType::Dac only) and Ok(()) for every other EndpointType, independently of and without altering check_functional_config_matches_ep_type's own REQ-RMAP-004 match behavior for a same-EndpointType PerEpConfigBlock/PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig pair; never panics for any EndpointType

requirements.title: check_compound_bundle_claim requires compound-wait support, ≥4 sequencers, and clear-non-safestate support together before accepting a "compound request support" claim
requirements.text: check_compound_bundle_claim(has_compound_wait, svr_sequencers_max, has_clear_non_safestate) returns Ok(()) only when has_compound_wait is true, svr_sequencers_max is greater than or equal to MIN_SEQUENCERS_FOR_COMPOUND_BUNDLE, and has_clear_non_safestate is true, all three simultaneously; returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) whenever any one of the three does not hold, including when none of them hold; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.2 ("Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of: Support of compound requests ... Implementation of at least four sequencers ... Clear all non-safestate requests from an EP request storage"), TC18.txt L2408-2413

requirements.title: MIN_SEQUENCERS_FOR_COMPOUND_BUNDLE fixes the "≥4 sequencers" threshold check_compound_bundle_claim enforces
requirements.text: MIN_SEQUENCERS_FOR_COMPOUND_BUNDLE equals 4; check_compound_bundle_claim rejects every svr_sequencers_max value strictly below MIN_SEQUENCERS_FOR_COMPOUND_BUNDLE (with the other two prerequisites otherwise satisfied) and accepts every svr_sequencers_max value at or above it, up to and including u8::MAX; never panics for any sampled svr_sequencers_max value
requirements.tc18: §12.2 ("Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of: Support of compound requests ... Implementation of at least four sequencers ... Clear all non-safestate requests from an EP request storage"), TC18.txt L2408-2413

requirements.title: crc32_tc18 implements the TC18 safe-point CRC-32 (poly 0xF4ACFB13, init/xorout 0xFFFFFFFF, reflected in/out), verified against an independent reference implementation of the same definition
requirements.text: crc32_tc18(data) matches a structurally independent reference implementation of the same poly=0xF4ACFB13/init=0xFFFFFFFF/xorout=0xFFFFFFFF/reflect-in/reflect-out CRC-32 definition across the empty input, the ASCII "123456789" check corpus, all-zero and all-0xFF 16-byte boundary inputs, and several other varied-length inputs including a full 0..=255 byte-value pattern
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Table 34 ("CRC32 Polynomial"), TC18.txt L4193-4208

requirements.title: crc32_tc18 never panics for arbitrary-length input, including empty input
requirements.text: crc32_tc18 returns a u32 without panicking for input slices of length 0 and for a range of other lengths up to at least 1000 bytes

requirements.title: crc32_tc18 is sensitive to input changes: different payloads and single-bit flips change the CRC
requirements.text: crc32_tc18 returns different values for two different sampled payloads, and returns a different value when a single bit of a given input is flipped, consistent with its role as an integrity check over safe-point frame bytes

requirements.title: CRC-32 coverage buffer assembly order (c-RCP rcp_e2e_compute_crc order)
requirements.text: build_crc32_coverage_buffer assembles the bytes crc32_tc18 is computed over in c-RCP's rcp_e2e_compute_crc order (c-RCP src/e2e.c:124-150): avtp_subtype (1 octet), the AVTPDU header's octet 1 (1 octet), a tu octet (0x01/0x00), the 8-octet stream_id and the 4-octet avtp_timestamp, both big-endian, then the full ACF header with acf_msg_length +1, then the payload; crc32_tc18 of that buffer equals the CRC wrap_for_header places for a self-consistent message, and changes when any covered byte changes
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("In Safe command mode a CRC32 is calculated per ACF type across specific fields of an AVTPDU header, ACF header, and the entire payload (except padding)."), TC18.txt L4191-4192

requirements.title: NTSCF coverage feeds a zero tu octet and a zero avtp_timestamp; TSCF feeds the real values
requirements.text: build_crc32_coverage_buffer (and every coverage path in e2e) feeds, for an NTSCF header, subtype 0x82, the header's octet 1, a 0x00 tu octet and four 0x00 avtp_timestamp octets, and for a TSCF header subtype 0x05, octet 1, the header's tu bit and its real avtp_timestamp. c-RCP parity (c-RCP src/e2e.c:140-148, :344-368): TC18 RC5 Figure 21 has no avtp_timestamp row and no tu column under NTSCF, but c-RCP feeds the zero stand-ins and this crate copies c-RCP for byte-for-byte interop (issue #152)
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Figure 20/21 (orange header-CRC fields), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5 p.88-89; c-RCP parity divergence for NTSCF

requirements.title: ACF header length-field pre-adjustment before CRC coverage
requirements.text: build_crc32_coverage_buffer encodes the covered ACF header's byte_message_info.acf_msg_length as the caller-supplied value plus one quadlet (4 octets), per this crate's working interpretation of the coverage rule's length-field pre-adjustment, and rejects a pre-adjusted value that overflows the 11-bit field width the same way encode_byte_message_info itself would
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("adding the CRC to the byte_msg_payload increases the acf_msg_length by 1"), TC18.txt L4272-4273

requirements.title: Coverage buffer covers the correct ACF_ABB vs ACF_GBB header shape
requirements.text: build_crc32_coverage_buffer's ACF header region, starting after the 15-octet header prefix, is exactly ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN bytes (byte_message_info, no message_timestamp) for AcfCoverageMessage::Abb and exactly ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN bytes (byte_message_info + the 8-byte message_timestamp) for AcfCoverageMessage::Gbb, immediately followed by the payload in both cases

requirements.title: Only the fragment train's final fragment (ms == false) carries a CRC
requirements.text: fragment_crc_expectation(ms) returns NotExpected for ms == true and Expected for ms == false; check_fragment_crc_placement(ms, crc_present) returns Ok(()) when ms == true and crc_present == false, and when ms == false and crc_present == true, and returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for the two invalid combinations (a CRC present on a non-final fragment, or absent on the final fragment) rather than silently ignoring either
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation. So, the CRC is only calculated once and will be transmitted in the last segment."), TC18.txt L4274-4275

requirements.title: CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble concatenates a fragment train's per-segment payloads in caller-supplied order
requirements.text: CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble(segments) returns the verbatim concatenation of segments in the order given, returns an empty combined payload for an empty segments slice, and never panics for any sampled segment slice, including a single-segment slice

requirements.title: Fragment-train CRC covers the first fragment's encoded ACF header plus the combined payload (c-RCP parity)
requirements.text: crc32_tc18_for_fragment_train(header, first_fragment, segments) returns compute_fragmented_crc over header's CRC inputs (NTSCF: tu false, avtp_timestamp 0), first_fragment's encoded ACF header exactly as acf::encode_acf_abb/encode_acf_gbb emit it (its own acf_msg_length, pad, ms and segment_num, no +1 quadlet), and the segments concatenated in order; build_crc32_coverage_buffer_for_fragment_train returns those same covered bytes; both are sensitive to every segment and propagate Err(RcpError::InvalidSize) when first_fragment cannot be encoded. c-RCP parity (c-RCP src/e2e.c:379-406, src/mock.c:2256-2263/2370): TC18-13.6-007 reads as a header for the whole unfragmented message (length and pad recomputed, then +1); this crate copies c-RCP's first-fragment model (issues #169, #170)
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation. So, the CRC is only calculated once and will be transmitted in the last segment."), TC18.txt L4274-4275

requirements.title: RequestKind's three MSB-tagged safety variants (0x8F/0x8B/0x8E) round-trip and equal 0x80 | their base kind
requirements.text: RequestKind::SafetyCompound, RequestKind::SafetyCompoundWait, and RequestKind::SafetyTriggered encode to 0x8F, 0x8B, and 0x8E respectively via to_u8, each exactly equal to 0x80 | the corresponding base kind's own to_u8 (RequestKind::Compound, RequestKind::CompoundWait, RequestKind::Triggered), round-trip through from_u8(kind.to_u8()) back to the same kind for all twelve RequestKind values, and from_u8 rejects nearby non-tagged bytes (0x80, 0x8A, 0x8C, 0x8D) with RcpError::InvalidParameter
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."), TC18.txt L1257-1259

requirements.title: RequestKind::is_safety_tagged is true only for the three MSB-tagged variants
requirements.text: RequestKind::is_safety_tagged() returns true for RequestKind::SafetyCompound, RequestKind::SafetyCompoundWait, and RequestKind::SafetyTriggered, and false for all nine other RequestKind values
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."), TC18.txt L1257-1259

requirements.title: Each safety-tagged variant resolves to the same execution-priority tier and exec-delay-timer selection as its own untagged base kind
requirements.text: execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::SafetyCompound) equals execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::Compound), execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::SafetyCompoundWait) equals execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::CompoundWait), and execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::SafetyTriggered) equals execution_priority_tier(RequestKind::Triggered); resolve_compound_exec_delay and resolve_trigger_exec_delay likewise resolve each safety-tagged variant identically to its own base kind, and never panic for any RequestKind value including the three new variants

requirements.title: check_watchdog_overflow_purge exempts safety-tagged requests and purges normal-priority requests only on overflow
requirements.text: check_watchdog_overflow_purge(kind, watchdog_overflowed) returns Ok(()) when watchdog_overflowed is false for every RequestKind, and when watchdog_overflowed is true and kind.is_safety_tagged() is true; returns Err(RcpError::RequestCanceled) when watchdog_overflowed is true and kind.is_safety_tagged() is false, for every one of the nine normal-priority RequestKind values; never panics for any sampled (kind, watchdog_overflowed) pair
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."), TC18.txt L1257-1259

requirements.title: purge_normal_priority_on_watchdog_overflow partitions a pending-request slice into kept and purged indices on watchdog overflow
requirements.text: purge_normal_priority_on_watchdog_overflow(pending, watchdog_overflowed) returns (vec![], vec![]) for an empty pending slice; returns every index in kept and an empty purged when watchdog_overflowed is false; when watchdog_overflowed is true, returns the indices of every safety-tagged entry in kept and every normal-priority entry in purged, in pending's own original relative order, correctly handling an all-safety-tagged slice (nothing purged) and an all-normal-priority slice (everything purged); never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."), TC18.txt L1257-1259

requirements.title: StreamWatchdogTimeout mirrors rx_wd_timeout_interval's width
requirements.text: StreamWatchdogTimeout wraps a u16 clock-tick count matching RequestStreamConfigEntry::rx_wd_timeout_interval's own encoded width; is_stream_watchdog_expired never panics for any (state, now_tick, timeout) input, including a now_tick preceding the last reset tick (saturating arithmetic)
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("WatchDog time out for this Stream in clock tics ... 0dec: WD is disabled"), TC18.txt L3232-3235

requirements.title: StreamWatchdogState liveness reset on every request
requirements.text: StreamWatchdogState::new(now_tick) records now_tick as the last reset tick; StreamWatchdogState::reset_on_request(now_tick) overwrites the previously recorded last reset tick with now_tick, modeling the per-stream 'reset on every request received' liveness rule rather than a periodic poll
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("the watchdog is reset with each request received from this RC Client"), TC18.txt L3301-3302

requirements.title: is_stream_watchdog_expired elapsed-ticks-vs-timeout check
requirements.text: is_stream_watchdog_expired(state, now_tick, timeout) returns false while now_tick - state.last_reset_tick() is less than timeout.0, true once it is at least timeout.0 (inclusive boundary), and correctly reflects a StreamWatchdogState::reset_on_request call pushing expiry back out; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("WatchDog time out for this Stream in clock tics ... 0dec: WD is disabled"), TC18.txt L3232-3235

requirements.title: evaluate_stream_watchdog is Alive when disabled or unexpired
requirements.text: evaluate_stream_watchdog returns StreamWatchdogOutcome::Alive when rx_wd_enable is false regardless of elapsed ticks, and when rx_wd_enable is true but the watchdog has not yet expired
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("WatchDog time out for this Stream in clock tics ... 0dec: WD is disabled"), TC18.txt L3232-3235

requirements.title: evaluate_stream_watchdog splits an expired watchdog by rx_wd_safestate_enable
requirements.text: evaluate_stream_watchdog returns StreamWatchdogOutcome::ExpiredSafestate when the watchdog has expired and rx_wd_safestate_enable is true, and StreamWatchdogOutcome::ExpiredNoSafestate when it has expired and rx_wd_safestate_enable is false
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("If a sequence error occurs a safe state may be enforced ... A similar mechanism can be additionally configured for the watchdog to ensure a continuous uninterrupted connection"), TC18.txt L3298-3302

requirements.title: StreamWatchdogOutcome::watchdog_overflowed is true for either expired variant
requirements.text: StreamWatchdogOutcome::watchdog_overflowed() returns false for Alive and true for both ExpiredNoSafestate and ExpiredSafestate, matching the plain bool check_watchdog_overflow_purge/purge_normal_priority_on_watchdog_overflow already take as watchdog_overflowed
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("If a sequence error occurs a safe state may be enforced ... A similar mechanism can be additionally configured for the watchdog to ensure a continuous uninterrupted connection"), TC18.txt L3298-3302

requirements.title: StreamWatchdogOutcome::drives_safestate is true only for ExpiredSafestate
requirements.text: StreamWatchdogOutcome::drives_safestate() returns true only for ExpiredSafestate and false for Alive and ExpiredNoSafestate
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("If a sequence error occurs a safe state may be enforced ... A similar mechanism can be additionally configured for the watchdog to ensure a continuous uninterrupted connection"), TC18.txt L3298-3302

requirements.title: evaluate_stream_watchdog never panics for any sampled input
requirements.text: evaluate_stream_watchdog does not panic across a sampled cross-product of reset ticks, now ticks, timeouts (including 0 and u16::MAX), and both bool flags
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("Request stream configuration"), TC18.txt L3222-3293

requirements.title: e2e_failure_scope selects DropRequest/LatchStream by rx_enforce_e2e
requirements.text: e2e_failure_scope(rx_enforce_e2e) returns E2eFailureScope::DropRequest when rx_enforce_e2e is false and E2eFailureScope::LatchStream when rx_enforce_e2e is true
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("0x000D.0 rx_enforce_crc: 0b stream is not blocked when CRC check at EP fails / 1b stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails and Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L3239-3243, cross-referenced by §13.6 (TC18.txt L4189-4190)

requirements.title: check_rx_enforce_e2e compares crc32_tc18(coverage_buffer) against expected_crc and reports scope on mismatch
requirements.text: check_rx_enforce_e2e(coverage_buffer, expected_crc, rx_enforce_e2e) returns Ok(()) when crc32_tc18(coverage_buffer) equals expected_crc for any rx_enforce_e2e value, and Err((RcpError::CrcError, e2e_failure_scope(rx_enforce_e2e))) when it does not; never panics for any sampled input
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("If a request is received by an endpoint that is in \"Safe command mode\" and the CRC does not match, the request is not executed, and an error response is generated with error code: CRC_ERROR. Depending on configuration safety measures might be taken (see parameter rx_enforce_crc in 12.7.7 Request stream configuration)."), TC18.txt L4188-4190

requirements.title: RcpError gains CrcError as a new variant for the CRC_ERROR error path, originally kept distinct from the now-retired legacy CrcMismatch sentinel
requirements.text: RcpError::CrcError is added as a new variant (not collapsed onto any of the eleven Milestone 2 TC18 error codes, nor onto the legacy CrcMismatch sentinel that motivated keeping it distinct at the time, since retired outright by Milestone 9's e2e REPLACE cutover), is distinct from other RcpError variants under equality, its Display text embeds the roadmap-named CRC_ERROR code following the enum's established "rcp/error: <CODE> - ..." message convention, and check_rx_enforce_e2e constructs it on a TC18 safe-point CRC-32 mismatch
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("the request is not executed, and an error response is generated with error code: CRC_ERROR"), TC18.txt L4188-4189

requirements.title: resolve_safe_state_mechanism selects HiZAllPins/SequencerDriven by rx_safety_measure
requirements.text: resolve_safe_state_mechanism(rx_safety_measure, rx_safestate_sequencer, rx_safe_sequencer_state) returns SafeStateMechanism::HiZAllPins when rx_safety_measure is false, and SafeStateMechanism::SequencerDriven wrapping safe_state_sequencer_gate(rx_safestate_sequencer, rx_safe_sequencer_state) when rx_safety_measure is true

requirements.title: safe_state_sequencer_gate builds a CompoundGateConfig from rx_safestate_sequencer/rx_safe_sequencer_state
requirements.text: safe_state_sequencer_gate(rx_safestate_sequencer, rx_safe_sequencer_state) returns a CompoundGateConfig whose sequencer_num equals rx_safestate_sequencer and whose start_state equals SequencerState(rx_safe_sequencer_state)

requirements.title: enter_sequencer_driven_safe_state writes a SequencerBank's named sequencer to its target state
requirements.text: enter_sequencer_driven_safe_state(bank, gate) writes bank's gate.sequencer_num entry to gate.start_state via SequencerBank::force_state and returns Ok(()) for an in-bounds sequencer_num, Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for an out-of-bounds one; never panics for any sampled input

requirements.title: SequencerBank::force_state writes unconditionally, bypassing the start-state race guard
requirements.text: SequencerBank::force_state(sequencer_num, new_state) overwrites the stored SequencerState at sequencer_num regardless of its current value (unlike advance_if_still_in_start_state, which only advances when the observed state still matches a gate's start_state), and returns Err(RcpError::SequencerNotKnown) for sequencer_num at or beyond svr_sequencers_max

requirements.title: OverflowOutcome models no-overflow / overflow-without-safestate / overflow-with-safestate
requirements.text: OverflowOutcome has exactly three variants (NoOverflow, OverflowNoSafestate, OverflowSafestate) constructed by evaluate_request_storage_overflow

requirements.title: OverflowOutcome::is_overflow/drives_safestate predicates agree with variant identity
requirements.text: OverflowOutcome::is_overflow() is false only for NoOverflow and true for both overflow variants; OverflowOutcome::drives_safestate() is true only for OverflowSafestate

requirements.title: evaluate_request_storage_overflow selects by storage_overflowed and rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable
requirements.text: evaluate_request_storage_overflow(storage_overflowed, rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable) returns OverflowOutcome::NoOverflow when storage_overflowed is false regardless of rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable, OverflowOutcome::OverflowSafestate when storage_overflowed is true and rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable is true, and OverflowOutcome::OverflowNoSafestate when storage_overflowed is true and rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable is false

requirements.title: SequenceEnforcementOutcome reports accept / discontinuity / enter_safe_state independently
requirements.text: SequenceEnforcementOutcome carries three independent booleans (accept, discontinuity, enter_safe_state) produced by SequenceTracker::evaluate (c-RCP rcp_e2e_seq_result_t)
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_sequence ... 0b: stream is not blocked upon out of order reception 1b: stream is blocked upon out of order reception and Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L3244-3248

requirements.title: SequenceEnforcementOutcome::is_rejected/drives_safestate predicates read the outcome's fields
requirements.text: SequenceEnforcementOutcome::is_rejected() is !accept and SequenceEnforcementOutcome::drives_safestate() is enter_safe_state, independently: an accepted frame with a discontinuity still drives safe state
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_sequence ... 0b: stream is not blocked upon out of order reception 1b: stream is blocked upon out of order reception and Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L3244-3248

requirements.title: evaluate_rx_enforce_seq applies c-RCP's mod-256 forward-distance window over a per-stream tracker
requirements.text: evaluate_rx_enforce_seq(tracker, rx_enforce_seq, rx_seq_safestate_enable, seq) returns exactly SequenceTracker::evaluate's outcome: accept when rx_enforce_seq is false or the 8-bit forward distance from the last accepted sequence_num is 1..=127 (so 255 -> 0 accepts and +128/duplicates reject), never panicking for any input
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_sequence ... 0b: stream is not blocked upon out of order reception 1b: stream is blocked upon out of order reception and Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L3244-3248

requirements.title: SafeStateAction models none / force-hi-Z / force-sequencer-state
requirements.text: SafeStateAction has exactly three variants (None, ForceHiZAllPins, ForceSequencerState(CompoundGateConfig)) constructed by resolve_safe_state_action

requirements.title: resolve_safe_state_action combines should_enter_safe_state with a resolved SafeStateMechanism
requirements.text: resolve_safe_state_action(should_enter_safe_state, mechanism) returns SafeStateAction::None when should_enter_safe_state is false regardless of mechanism; otherwise returns SafeStateAction::ForceHiZAllPins for SafeStateMechanism::HiZAllPins and SafeStateAction::ForceSequencerState(gate) for SafeStateMechanism::SequencerDriven(gate); never panics for any sampled input

requirements.title: LIN_MAX_DATA matches the real LIN 2.x per-frame data ceiling
requirements.text: lin::LIN_MAX_DATA == 8, LIN 2.x's own physical ceiling stated directly as this module's own constant (originally reused as crate::linbr::LIN_MAX_DATA, the value's original home before the linbr REPLACE cutover deleted that legacy Zone/Command-coupled module in Milestone 9, no longer exists to import from), without reusing any of the legacy linbr::LinBridge::send's surrounding PID-derivation logic

requirements.title: LinFrameTransfer round-trips PID+data bytes through encode/decode and never panics
requirements.text: LinFrameTransfer::encode/LinFrameTransfer::decode round-trip any client-supplied pid byte and data bytes (up to LIN_MAX_DATA bytes), carrying both unparsed and unvalidated for parity or checksum content, and decode never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 ("lin request format"), TC18.txt L5719-5736

requirements.title: LinFrameTransfer::decode rejects an empty slice with no PID byte present
requirements.text: LinFrameTransfer::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for an empty byte slice, since no PID byte is present to decode
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 ("lin request format"), TC18.txt L5719-5736

requirements.title: LinFrameTransfer::decode rejects data bytes exceeding LIN_MAX_DATA and accepts exactly LIN_MAX_DATA
requirements.text: LinFrameTransfer::decode returns Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) when the bytes following the PID byte exceed LIN_MAX_DATA in length, and succeeds when they equal LIN_MAX_DATA exactly, matching the real LIN 2.x per-frame data ceiling the legacy linbr::LinBridge::send already enforced

requirements.title: LinFrameTransferResult round-trips response data bytes through encode/decode, enforces LIN_MAX_DATA, and never panics
requirements.text: LinFrameTransferResult::encode/LinFrameTransferResult::decode round-trip any data byte sequence up to and including LIN_MAX_DATA bytes without interpreting its contents, decode returns Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) for longer input, and decode never panics for any input length

requirements.title: LinFunctionalConfig's layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Lin cross-layer rule
requirements.text: LinFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Lin that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: LinRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 LIN request after evt[2:0] validation
requirements.text: LinRequest's two variants (Plain(LinFrameTransfer), ConfigWrite) give an incoming LIN request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike AdcRequest::Plain (no payload struct at all) and PwmInRequest::Plain (a raw, uninterpreted byte transfer, since PWM_IN's own request-payload framing is unconfirmed), LinRequest::Plain reuses this module's own pre-existing, already-confirmed LinFrameTransfer::decode, since TC18 §13.7.10.1 states the LIN EP sends the bytes provided by the RC Client in byte_msg_payload on the bus and this module's own TC18 reconciliation note already established that payload's pid+data byte layout with nothing left to bridge
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (LIN is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.10.1 LIN EP request handling ("It sends the bytes provided by the RC Client in the byte_msg_payload on the bus as response to a pending read request."), TC18.txt L5691-5692

requirements.title: LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain/ConfigWrite, propagates LinFrameTransfer::decode's own ShortFrame/PayloadTooLarge errors on a Plain request, and rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, never panicking
requirements.text: LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode decodes a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request's payload bytes as a LinFrameTransfer via LinFrameTransfer::decode, propagating that function's own Result rather than inventing a second validation of the same bytes -- Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for an empty payload (no PID byte present) and Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) for data beyond LIN_MAX_DATA bytes. A ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request is recognized without attempting to interpret its payload (full TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload decoding is deferred, not silently guessed at). Every Reserved sub_opcode value returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and crate::i2c::I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::adc::AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/crate::pwm::PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's identical refusal of their own table's reserved code; never panics for any sub_opcode/payload combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: FrameFormat round-trips through to_u8/from_u8 and its classification helpers partition all six variants
requirements.text: FrameFormat::to_u8/FrameFormat::from_u8 round-trip each of the six CBFF/CEFF/FBFF/FEFF/XL-classical/XL-new variants, and exactly one of is_classical/is_fd/is_xl is true for each variant
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 Table 57 ("can frame formats"), TC18.txt L5863-5872

requirements.title: FrameFormat::from_u8 rejects any byte outside 0..=5
requirements.text: FrameFormat::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte value outside 0..=5, and never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 Table 57 ("can frame formats"), TC18.txt L5863-5872

requirements.title: CLASSICAL_CAN_MAX_DATA and CAN_FD_MAX_PAYLOAD match the real classical CAN 2.0 and CAN FD physical data-length ceilings
requirements.text: can::CLASSICAL_CAN_MAX_DATA == 8 and can::CAN_FD_MAX_PAYLOAD == 64, both classical CAN 2.0/CAN FD's own physical ceilings stated directly as this module's own constants (canbr::CAN_FD_MAX_PAYLOAD, the value's original home before the canbr REPLACE cutover deleted that legacy Zone/Command-coupled module in Milestone 9, no longer exists to import from)

requirements.title: CanDataFrame round-trips format+id+data through encode/decode, and FrameFormat's id-width/data-ceiling helpers match the real base/extended and classical/FD physical facts
requirements.text: CanDataFrame::encode/CanDataFrame::decode round-trip any of the four non-XL FrameFormat variants together with an arbitration id within that format's real id width (CAN_STANDARD_ID_MAX for base formats, CAN_EXTENDED_ID_MAX for extended formats per FrameFormat::is_extended_id) and data up to that format's own FrameFormat::max_data_len ceiling

requirements.title: CanDataFrame::decode rejects short input, XL format tags, out-of-width arbitration ids, and data exceeding the format's ceiling, and never panics
requirements.text: CanDataFrame::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input shorter than 5 bytes, Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when the decoded format is an XL variant or the arbitration id exceeds the width that format allows, Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) when data exceeds the format's FrameFormat::max_data_len ceiling, and never panics for any input length

requirements.title: CanXlSubHeader round-trips its 6 opaque bytes through encode/decode and CAN_XL_SUB_HEADER_LEN/CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD match ROADMAP.md's stated CAN XL ceilings
requirements.text: CanXlSubHeader::encode/CanXlSubHeader::decode round-trip any 6-byte value without interpreting its contents, decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input shorter than CAN_XL_SUB_HEADER_LEN, and can::CAN_XL_SUB_HEADER_LEN == 6 while can::CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD == 2048, matching ROADMAP.md Milestone 7's own stated CAN XL sub-header length and payload ceiling
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CanXlFrame round-trips format+sub_header+payload through encode/decode for both XL variants
requirements.text: CanXlFrame::encode/CanXlFrame::decode round-trip FrameFormat::XlClassical and FrameFormat::XlNew together with any CanXlSubHeader and any payload up to CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD bytes
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CanXlFrame::decode rejects short input and non-XL format tags, and never panics
requirements.text: CanXlFrame::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input too short to contain the format tag plus a full CAN_XL_SUB_HEADER_LEN-byte sub-header, Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when the decoded format is not FrameFormat::XlClassical or FrameFormat::XlNew, and never panics for any input length
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CanXlFrame::decode rejects payload exceeding CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD and accepts exactly CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD
requirements.text: CanXlFrame::decode returns Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) when the payload following the sub-header exceeds CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD (2048) bytes in length, and succeeds when it equals CAN_XL_MAX_PAYLOAD exactly
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CanXlCombinedPayload::assemble concatenates caller-supplied fragment-train segments in the order given
requirements.text: CanXlCombinedPayload::assemble concatenates a slice of caller-supplied, already-ordered byte-segment slices verbatim in the order given, yields an empty combined payload for an empty segment slice, and never panics for any input including empty per-segment payloads, mirroring crate::e2e::CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble's own caller-supplied-ordering discipline for the same Milestone 8 forward dependency

requirements.title: CanFunctionalConfig's layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Can cross-layer rule
requirements.text: CanFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Can that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: The NIBBLE_TO_5B 4b/5b data code-group table has 16 distinct, 5-bit-wide entries
requirements.text: iseled::NIBBLE_TO_5B contains 16 entries, one per 4-bit nibble value, each fitting in 5 bits with no duplicate code group across the table

requirements.title: encode_4b5b/decode_4b5b round-trip any byte sequence, decode_4b5b rejects odd-length or invalid-code-group input, and never panics
requirements.text: iseled::encode_4b5b/iseled::decode_4b5b round-trip any byte slice including empty input through NIBBLE_TO_5B's data code groups; decode_4b5b returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for odd-length input, Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any byte not among NIBBLE_TO_5B's 16 valid code groups, and never panics for any input length

requirements.title: IseledFrame's chain_address/command/data fields round-trip through encode with no length ceiling on data
requirements.text: IseledFrame::encode serializes chain_address, command, and data unmodified in that order, and IseledFrame accepts data of any length

requirements.title: IseledFrame::decode round-trips encode's output, rejects input shorter than 2 bytes, and never panics
requirements.text: IseledFrame::decode(IseledFrame::encode(frame)) reproduces the original frame for any chain_address/command/data combination; IseledFrame::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input shorter than 2 bytes and never panics for any input length

requirements.title: IseledFrame::encode_line/decode_line compose IseledFrame::encode/decode with encode_4b5b/decode_4b5b and propagate the latter's errors
requirements.text: IseledFrame::decode_line(frame.encode_line()) reproduces the original frame, and IseledFrame::decode_line propagates Err(RcpError::ShortFrame)/Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) from decode_4b5b unchanged for malformed line-coded input

requirements.title: iseled_frame_crc8 is a deterministic function of an IseledFrame's own bytes, computed independently of crate::e2e::crc32_tc18
requirements.text: iseled_frame_crc8 returns the same IseledFrameCrc value for the same IseledFrame content and a different value when frame content differs, and this crate's native ISELED CRC computation shares no code path with crate::e2e::crc32_tc18's own RCP-level safe-point CRC-32

requirements.title: IseledDeviceResponse carries one daisy-chain device's chain_address and its own response data bytes
requirements.text: IseledDeviceResponse's chain_address and data fields are preserved unmodified when constructed and compared

requirements.title: iseled_collect_resp preserves caller-supplied per-device structure and order, yields an empty result for empty input, and never panics
requirements.text: iseled_collect_resp(per_device) produces an IseledCollectedResponse whose contents equal per_device in the same order, with no reordering, deduplication, or flattening of distinct devices' responses; an empty per_device slice yields an empty IseledCollectedResponse, and the function never panics for any input, mirroring crate::can::CanXlCombinedPayload::assemble's own caller-supplied-ordering discipline

requirements.title: IseledFunctionalConfig's native_crc_enabled field models the native ISELED CRC's optional, additive-only presence
requirements.text: IseledFunctionalConfig::native_crc_enabled defaults to false and can be independently set to true without altering whether crate::e2e::crc32_tc18's RCP-level safe-point CRC applies
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.1 ("The optional CRC generation as specified in the ISLED standard can be enabled."), TC18.txt L5910-5911

requirements.title: IseledFunctionalConfig's layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Iseled cross-layer rule
requirements.text: IseledFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Iseled that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: MdioAddressingMode round-trips through to_u8/from_u8 across the full 2-bit 0..=3 range
requirements.text: mdio::MdioAddressingMode::from_u8(mode.to_u8()) reproduces the original mode for all four variants (Clause22, Clause45, Spare2, Spare3), and the four variants' to_u8 values are exactly 0..=3

requirements.title: MdioAddressingMode::from_u8 rejects any wire byte outside the 2-bit 0..=3 range
requirements.text: mdio::MdioAddressingMode::from_u8 returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any input byte greater than 3, and never panics

requirements.title: MdioAddressingMode::is_unallocated_slot is true only for Spare2/Spare3 and the type defaults to Clause22
requirements.text: mdio::MdioAddressingMode::is_unallocated_slot returns true only for Spare2/Spare3 and false for Clause22/Clause45; MdioAddressingMode::default() is Clause22, which is_unallocated_slot reports as false

requirements.title: MdioFunctionalConfig carries only its addressing_mode field, defaults to Clause22, and its layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Mdio cross-layer rule
requirements.text: mdio::MdioFunctionalConfig::default().addressing_mode is MdioAddressingMode::Clause22; MdioFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Mdio that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: MdioTransfer's raw byte stream round-trips through encode/decode for any input and never panics
requirements.text: mdio::MdioTransfer::decode(transfer.encode()) reproduces the original bytes for any byte slice including empty input, and MdioTransfer::decode never panics for any input length

requirements.title: MdioTransferResult's raw byte stream round-trips through encode/decode for any input and never panics
requirements.text: mdio::MdioTransferResult::decode(result.encode()) reproduces the original bytes for any byte slice including empty input, and MdioTransferResult::decode never panics for any input length

requirements.title: MdioRequest enumerates the decoded shape of a Row-2 MDIO request after evt[2:0] validation, wrapping an already-decoded MdioTransfer
requirements.text: MdioRequest's two variants (Plain(MdioTransfer), ConfigWrite) give an incoming MDIO request's decoded shape after its evt.sub_opcode has been validated against evt_row2_kind_of's Table 33 Row-2 rule; MdioRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode is the request-decode entry point that performs that validation and dispatch. Unlike I2cRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/LinRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/AdcRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/PwmInRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode/UartRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode (each of which take raw byte_msg_payload bytes and decode them internally), MdioRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode takes an already-decoded MdioTransfer, matching CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's own shape rather than those five siblings' -- MdioTransfer already has its own dedicated decode entry point (MdioTransfer::decode, pre-existing this item and unchanged by it), so this evt[2:0]-classification entry point does not re-derive that byte-layout logic a second time internally
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33's Row-2 row (MDIO is one of its eight endpoint types), TC18.txt L4085-4092, and §13.7.13.3 MDIO request handling, TC18.txt L6065-6066

requirements.title: MdioRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode accepts Plain and ConfigWrite, rejects Reserved sub_opcodes with UnsupportedCmd, and keeps the Ok(Self::ConfigWrite) precedent rather than CanRequest/IseledRequest's ConfigWriteNotImplemented departure, never panicking
requirements.text: MdioRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode wraps the caller-supplied MdioTransfer unchanged in MdioRequest::Plain for a Plain (sub_opcode 0) request, and returns Ok(MdioRequest::ConfigWrite) without interpreting the supplied MdioTransfer for a ConfigWrite (sub_opcode 7) request -- deliberately keeping the Ok(Self::ConfigWrite) precedent I2cRequest/LinRequest/AdcRequest/PwmInRequest/UartRequest each follow rather than following CanRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's/IseledRequest::from_evt_sub_opcode's own Err(RcpError::ConfigWriteNotImplemented) departure, because MdioTransfer::decode is infallible and interprets no structure at all (every byte slice is a valid MdioTransfer, matching I2cByteTransfer's own raw pass-through discipline), so unlike CanDataFrame/IseledFrame a caller can honestly construct an MdioTransfer from a genuine TC18 §12.7.1 config-write payload with zero misrepresentation -- the 'no caller can honestly construct one' pressure that drove CAN's/ISELED's own departure does not apply to MDIO. Every Reserved sub_opcode value (evt[2:0] in 001b..=110b, or any value outside the 3-bit field's representable range) returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), matching TC18 Table 33's Row-2 error-code requirement and every prior Row-2 endpoint-type module's identical refusal of their own table's reserved code. Never panics for any sub_opcode/transfer combination
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: ... used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092

requirements.title: SleepCmdRequest's fixed 0xA5 discriminant round-trips through encode/decode
requirements.text: wakeup::SleepCmdRequest::encode always produces the single byte 0xA5 (wakeup::SleepCmdRequest::DISCRIMINANT), and wakeup::SleepCmdRequest::decode reproduces the original value from that byte
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("SleepCMD is coded as 0xA5."), TC18.txt L4565

requirements.title: SleepCmdRequest::decode rejects short input and any non-0xA5 first byte
requirements.text: wakeup::SleepCmdRequest::decode returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for an empty slice and Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) for any first byte other than 0xA5, and never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("SleepCMD is coded as 0xA5."), TC18.txt L4565

requirements.title: WakeSourcePinMask round-trips through encode/decode and rejects short input
requirements.text: wakeup::WakeSourcePinMask::decode(mask.encode()) reproduces the original mask for any u32 value, ignores trailing bytes beyond the first four, returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input shorter than WAKE_SOURCE_PIN_MASK_LEN, and never panics for any input
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 ("wake-up control - functional configuration"), TC18.txt L4497-4515

requirements.title: WakeupTriggerConfig round-trips through encode/decode, rejects short input, and defaults to no armed pins
requirements.text: wakeup::WakeupTriggerConfig::decode(config.encode()) reproduces the original config, returns Err(RcpError::ShortFrame) for input shorter than WAKE_SOURCE_PIN_MASK_LEN, and WakeupTriggerConfig::default().wake_enable is WakeSourcePinMask(0)
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 ("wake-up control - functional configuration"), TC18.txt L4497-4515

requirements.title: evaluate_wake_source_signals reports only wake-source pins that are both armed and observed
requirements.text: wakeup::evaluate_wake_source_signals returns a WakeSourceSignals whose fired mask equals config.wake_enable bitwise-AND observed, WakeSourceSignals::any_fired is true only when that mask is nonzero, and the function never panics for any input

requirements.title: WakeupFunctionalConfig defaults to no armed pins and its layer tag matches crate::regmap's EndpointType::Wakeup cross-layer rule
requirements.text: wakeup::WakeupFunctionalConfig::default().trigger is WakeupTriggerConfig::default(); WakeupFunctionalConfig::layer_tag produces a crate::regmap::PerEpTypeFunctionalConfig tagged EndpointType::Wakeup that satisfies crate::regmap::check_functional_config_matches_ep_type against a generic PerEpConfigBlock of the same ep_type, and is rejected by functional_config_matches_ep_type against a mismatched ep_type

requirements.title: request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd composes a decoded SleepCmdRequest with crate::powerstate::try_enter_power_mode without duplicating its transition or gate logic
requirements.text: wakeup::request_sleep_via_sleep_cmd(SleepCmdRequest, from, to, gate) returns exactly what crate::powerstate::try_enter_power_mode(from, to, gate) returns for every sampled (from, to, gate) combination, and never panics
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("To bring the RC Server implementation into sleep mode the RC Client has to send a specific request to the WakeUp endpoint."), TC18.txt L4546-4547

requirements.title: wake_source_signals_trigger_handshake composes a fired WakeSourceSignals with crate::powerstate::send_wakeup_request, rejecting when nothing fired
requirements.text: wakeup::wake_source_signals_trigger_handshake returns Err(RcpError::RequestRejected) when WakeSourceSignals::any_fired is false regardless of handshake state, and otherwise delegates to crate::powerstate::send_wakeup_request(state), advancing WakeUpHandshakeState::Idle to RequestSent and rejecting every other starting state; never panics for any input

requirements.title: FragmentReassemblyBuffer::new and fragmentation_supported reflect the rx_stream_max_request_size sentinel
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::new(0) constructs successfully but fragmentation_supported() returns false; any nonzero bound makes fragmentation_supported() true; a newly constructed buffer is not in_progress and has no segments

requirements.title: accept_fragment rejects every fragment on a fragmentation-unsupported stream
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment on a buffer constructed with rx_stream_max_request_size == 0 always returns Err(RcpError::UnsupportedCmd), regardless of the fragment's own ms/segment_num, and leaves the buffer not in_progress

requirements.title: accept_fragment enforces a strictly-incrementing, zero-based segment_num sequence on ms=1 fragments
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment shall, for a fragment whose ByteMessageInfo::ms is true, read the raw read_size_segment field as segment_num regardless of ByteMessageInfo::op (c-RCP parity: rcp_fragment_reassembler_feed, c-RCP src/fragment.c:158-192) and accept it only when it equals the next expected value: 0 for the first ms=1 fragment of a train, then exactly one more than the previously accepted ms=1 fragment; a gap, duplicate, out-of-order, or non-zero first value returns Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) and leaves the buffer's prior state unchanged

requirements.title: accept_fragment enforces the rx_stream_max_request_size combined-payload bound
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment returns Err(RcpError::PayloadTooLarge) and leaves the buffer's prior state unchanged whenever accepting the fragment would push the train's combined payload length past the configured rx_stream_max_request_size, and accepts a fragment landing exactly at that bound

requirements.title: accept_fragment reports Continuing/Complete by ms, and combined_payload matches CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble
requirements.text: fragment::FragmentReassemblyBuffer::accept_fragment returns Ok(FragmentAcceptOutcome::Continuing) when ByteMessageInfo::ms is true and Ok(FragmentAcceptOutcome::Complete) when it is false, including for a single-fragment train; combined_payload() after any sequence of accepted fragments equals crate::e2e::CombinedFragmentPayload::assemble of the same segments in arrival order
