requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Each response stream configured is assigned to at least one request stream... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2570-2572

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT does not trigger when every used endpoint and configured request stream is plausibly associated
requirements.text: lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK when every endpoint with ep_used set has has_stream_assoc set and every request stream with configured set has has_response_stream set, and shall treat a NULL snapshot as inconsistent rather than vacuously plausible. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-007; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced. Plausibility check contains a check that: Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association..."), TC18.txt L2566-2568

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED to HW_CONFIGURED is gated by the HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT check
requirements.text: lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED only when lifecycle::check_hw_cfg returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK for the supplied snapshot, and shall otherwise leave *state unchanged and return the check's RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT result. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-008; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("...the life-cycle state can be advanced to HW_CONFIGURED... Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."), TC18.txt L2544-2550

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED is gated by the RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT check
requirements.text: lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED only when lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK for the supplied snapshot, and shall otherwise leave *state unchanged and return the check's RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT result. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-009; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...the life-cycle state can be advanced to RCP_CONFIGURED... Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2562-2572

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED to HW_UNCONFIGURED demotion is unconditional
requirements.text: lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK regardless of the supplied snapshot, including a NULL snapshot. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-010; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.) Snapshot-independence only: writer authorization (REQ-LIFECYCLE-031/037) and idleness (REQ-LIFECYCLE-022) are still required.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Besides advancing the state it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request to the server functional configuration entry svr_lifecycle_state." -- no plausibility gate is described for this direction), TC18.txt L2574-2577

requirements.title: RCP_CONFIGURED to HW_UNCONFIGURED full-reset demotion is unconditional
requirements.text: lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK regardless of the supplied snapshot, including a NULL snapshot. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-011; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.) Snapshot-independence only: writer authorization (REQ-LIFECYCLE-031/037) and idleness (REQ-LIFECYCLE-022) are still required.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Besides advancing the state it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request..."), TC18.txt L2574-2577 -- NOTE: TC18's Figure 17 state-transition chart additionally gates this specific demotion on all other EPs being idle ("other EPs are not Idle -> send error response EPs_NOT_IDLE", TC18.txt L2501-2502); CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (issue #456): that gate IS implemented -- rcp_lifecycle_transition()'s RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_UNCONFIGURED branch enforces it via the all_other_eps_idle parameter (src/lifecycle.c:189, `if (!all_other_eps_idle) return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE;`), landed under REQ-LIFECYCLE-022; see that requirement for the separate, still-open gap (EPs_NOT_IDLE has no corresponding numbered wire error code in §12.9.6's table, so the local error is not yet wired to a wire response) -- not this requirement, which documents the snapshot-independence of the transition itself

requirements.title: Unmodeled lifecycle transitions are rejected
requirements.text: CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (issue #455): lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION and leave *state unchanged for any requested transition other than HW_UNCONFIGURED->HW_CONFIGURED, HW_CONFIGURED->RCP_CONFIGURED, RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_CONFIGURED, HW_CONFIGURED->HW_UNCONFIGURED, RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_UNCONFIGURED, or a same-state transition -- including HW_UNCONFIGURED->RCP_CONFIGURED, the one genuinely unmodeled topology. This entry previously named RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_CONFIGURED as a second rejected example -- wrong: TC18 Figure 17 explicitly diagrams that arrow ("Root Client or (stream/bb_ID & no root configured) access via EP0 to set state to HW_CONFIGURED & all other EPs are Idle -> send positive response"), which lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition simply failed to implement (issue #455, see REQ-LIFECYCLE-039, now fixed) -- not a case TC18 itself models as rejected. The claim below that Figure 17's own chart names "no other transitions" was the same error restated as a citation; corrected accordingly. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-012; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("A request to advance the state directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response."), TC18.txt L2545 -- this sentence's own scope is HW_UNCONFIGURED->RCP_CONFIGURED specifically (skipping HW_CONFIGURED entirely), the one transition genuinely absent from Figure 17's own chart, TC18.txt L2432-2517 (page 51 of the current RC5 PDF) -- verified at pixel resolution against the diagram image directly, not just this cached text extraction, before correcting this entry 2026-08-16 (issue #455).

requirements.title: A same-state lifecycle transition is a no-op success
requirements.text: lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK and leave *state unchanged whenever target equals the current *state, for all three lifecycle states, regardless of the supplied snapshot. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-013; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED accepts an ACF_ABB request at the discovery byte_bus_id under NTSCF
requirements.text: lifecycle::should_accept shall return true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED when avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF, acf_msg_type is RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB, and byte_bus_id equals RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-014; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted... Within the stream only requests ACF_ABB are supported for configuration, and all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00."), TC18.txt L2539-2541

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED silently drops any misaddressed frame, and rejects (with a response) a non-ABB request correctly addressed to EP0
requirements.text: lifecycle::should_accept shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED whenever avtp_subtype is not RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF or byte_bus_id does not equal RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID. When avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF and byte_bus_id equals RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID but acf_msg_type is not RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB, lifecycle::should_accept shall instead return RCP_LIFECYCLE_REJECT, not RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP -- this entry's own original text (predating the REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 fix, which widened lifecycle::should_accept's return type from a boolean to the three-way rcp_lifecycle_accept_t ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT) claimed a uniform silent-drop outcome across all three conditions; the acf_msg_type condition alone, with the other two satisfied, now produces a REJECT with an RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED wire response instead, per REQ-LIFECYCLE-033. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-015; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted... Within the stream only requests ACF_ABB are supported for configuration, and all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00."), TC18.txt L2539-2541 -- governs the avtp_subtype and byte_bus_id conditions only (both still produce RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP); the acf_msg_type condition no longer does, since TC18 §12.7's more specific EP0-scoped rule ("REQUEST_REJECTED", TC18.txt L2830) was found to override §12.3.1.1's general "all other requests are dropped without further response" for exactly the case of a non-ABB message correctly addressed to EP0 -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 (implemented) for the fix and full reconciliation between the two sections.

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED drops any TSCF-headed frame regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: lifecycle::should_accept shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED whenever avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF, regardless of the value of time_sync_supported. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-016; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted and all others are dropped without further response." -- TSCF is one of those "others"), TC18.txt L2539

requirements.title: RCP_CONFIGURED applies the ordinary TSCF/time-sync drop rule; HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF unconditionally
requirements.text: lifecycle::should_accept shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED whenever rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() would return true for the given time_sync_supported and avtp_subtype, and shall otherwise return true for that state. RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED instead drops every TSCF-headed frame unconditionally, regardless of what rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() would return -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-028 for that stricter, separately-tracked rule. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own formal "shall" text and title previously claimed the ordinary rule applied to HW_CONFIGURED too, which the code has never done since REQ-LIFECYCLE-028 landed (src/lifecycle.c:245, `if (avtp_subtype == RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF) return RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP;`, inside the HW_CONFIGURED branch, unconditional) -- only this entry's own citation footnote acknowledged the divergence in prose; the normative text did not. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-017; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140 -- same general rule as REQ-AVTP-014, now correctly scoped to RCP_CONFIGURED only; TC18 §12.3.1.2 separately specifies HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF unconditionally regardless of time-sync support, formally tracked at REQ-LIFECYCLE-028

requirements.title: HW_GENERIC fields are writable only via the discovery stream while HW_UNCONFIGURED, and read-only thereafter
requirements.text: lifecycle::is_field_writable shall return true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC only when state is RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and writer.via_discovery_stream is true, shall return false for that field kind for any other writer context while still RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, and shall return false for that field kind unconditionally in both RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously said HW_UNCONFIGURED writability held "for every writer context", which stopped being true once REQ-LIFECYCLE-026/035's fix (src/lifecycle.c:308) gated it on writer.via_discovery_stream -- the HW_CONFIGURED/RCP_CONFIGURED read-only half of this entry's own text was, and remains, correct. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-018; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("In this state access to the HW configuration of the RC Server shall have been concluded and as such all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2553-2554; §12.3.1.1 ("All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery."), TC18.txt L2537, the basis for the HW_UNCONFIGURED via_discovery_stream gate (REQ-LIFECYCLE-026/035)

requirements.title: FUNCTIONAL_W fields require an authorized writer once HW_CONFIGURED or RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: lifecycle::is_field_writable shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED for every writer context; shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0 or writer.via_owning_stream is true; and shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true -- one condition wider than the RCP_CONFIGURED case. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously claimed HW_CONFIGURED writability held "for every writer context", contradicted by both the code (REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization gate, src/lifecycle.c:284-291,311-319) and this project's own test (test_lifecycle.c's test_functional_w_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream()). (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-019; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2581-2582, L2601-2602; §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt L2552), the basis for HW_CONFIGURED's wider via_discovery_stream allowance (REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036)

requirements.title: FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR fields require the same authorized writer as FUNCTIONAL_W while HW_CONFIGURED, and are permanently locked once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: lifecycle::is_field_writable shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED for every writer context, including one with both via_root_client_ep0 and via_owning_stream set; shall return true unconditionally in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED; and shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true -- the same gate REQ-LIFECYCLE-019 applies to FUNCTIONAL_W. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously claimed unconditional HW_CONFIGURED writability, contradicted by REQ-LIFECYCLE-036's later fix (src/lifecycle.c:321-335), which gated this same branch identically to FUNCTIONAL_W's own HW_CONFIGURED case. The RCP_CONFIGURED permanent-lock half of this entry's own text was, and remains, correct. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-020; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables (W*: write prohibited in depending on lifecycle state.)"), TC18.txt L2601-2602 -- TC18's W* marker is general; c-RCP's split into FUNCTIONAL_W (conditionally writable via authorization) versus FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR (unconditionally locked once RCP_CONFIGURED) is this implementation's own refinement of which W* fields fall into which case, not itself named in the cited text

requirements.title: lifecycle::LifecycleError::message returns a unique human-readable message
requirements.text: lifecycle::LifecycleError::message shall return a distinct, non-empty, non-NULL string for each of RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK, RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT, RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT, and RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-021; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state change is refused with EPs_NOT_IDLE while any other endpoint is busy
requirements.text: PARTIAL, CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (issue #455): a pixel-level re-transcription of TC18 Figure 17 (page 51 of the current RC5 PDF, not just the pre-existing text extraction, which renders this diagram too poorly to trust for a design decision) found this entry's own prior verification pass had misattributed which arrow the idle-gate belongs to. The EPs_NOT_IDLE gate actually applies to exactly THREE transitions, not two: the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED demotion ("Root Client or (stream/bb_ID & no root configured) access via EP0 to set state to HW_CONFIGURED & all other EPs are Idle -> send positive response" -- previously not modeled at all in lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition, now added), the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, and the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset ("...& other EPs are not Idle -> send error response EPs_NOT_IDLE"). The HW_UNCONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED advance -- previously (incorrectly) idle-gated -- is NOT: its own label ("Request on discovery stream to set HW_CONFIGURED state & HW_config consistent -> send positive response") makes no mention of idleness at all; the wording this entry's prior text attributed to it in fact belongs to the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED demotion's own, textually distinct, label. The HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance's own label still makes no mention of idleness and remains correctly NOT gated. lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition now takes an all_other_eps_idle parameter and rejects with RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE for all three correctly-gated transitions when false. STILL OPEN (unchanged by this correction, out of this entry's own scope): a closer re-reading also found the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset's own diagram label ("Request on (discovery stream or known stream_id/bb_id and no root client set) or root client to set HW_UNCONFIGURED state -> send positive response") makes no mention of idleness either, yet lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition idle-gates it anyway -- a possible FOURTH citation/behavior question in the same family as this entry's own, deliberately NOT changed by issue #455 (whose own scope names exactly three findings) and flagged here for a future issue rather than force-fixed without the same independent confirmation this entry's other claims received. Not fully IMPLEMENTED: TC18's own diagram names the idle-gate failure outcome "EPs_NOT_IDLE" but that name maps to none of the seventeen numbered wire error codes errors.h models (§12.9.6's own table) -- a genuine TC18 inconsistency this library cannot resolve by inventing a mapping, so RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE remains a local-only lifecycle error code, not yet wired to a wire response. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-022; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2492-L2495 and L2504-L2506 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338): the cached TC18.txt's own lifecycle-diagram is Figure 17 in the current RC5 baseline ("Figure 17 - RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517), not "Figure 16" as this citation previously said -- Figure 16 in the current RC5 text is an unrelated diagram ("Cancellation of a single, specific request", TC18.txt L2158). Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the discovery claimant's stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the enforcement point this entry originally named was wrong -- lifecycle::should_accept is a frame-admission filter (subtype/msg-type/byte_bus_id only), not where TC18's own write-authorization rules live in this codebase (that is lifecycle::is_field_writable, the same layering REQ-LIFECYCLE-027/030/036 already established). The real gap was RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED branch admitting any writer unconditionally, with no authorization concept at all. Fixed: HW_GENERIC is now writable in HW_UNCONFIGURED only when writer.via_discovery_stream is set, matching TC18 §12.3.1.1's "All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery." Deriving via_discovery_stream from a real frame's stream_id against rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) is caller composition, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the same division of responsibility REQ-LIFECYCLE-027's via_non_unicast_frame member already established for this library. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-026; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: Write requests are accepted only from unicast frames
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2 and §12.3.1.3 each state (once per lifecycle state) that a write request is accepted only when carried in a unicast frame. rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t gained a via_non_unicast_frame member (l2.h's new rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() -- REQ-L2-011 -- is the primitive an integrator uses to classify a real frame's destination MAC into it), and lifecycle::is_field_writable now ANDs !writer.via_non_unicast_frame into every kind/state that would otherwise be writable, uniformly across HW_GENERIC, FUNCTIONAL_W and FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR. rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() gained a matching via_unicast parameter so its one real derivation path plumbs the same classification through. lifecycle::should_accept deliberately still takes no destination-MAC input: TC18's rule is scoped to write requests specifically, not general frame admission, so gating happens only at the field_writable() layer where the write path already lives, not at should_accept()'s frame-admission layer. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-027; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF-headed AVTPDUs regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.2 (whose own printed heading confusingly repeats "HW_UNCONFIGURED" -- verified against the primary-source PDF directly to rule out an extraction artifact; the section's actual content is unambiguously about HW_CONFIGURED, distinct from the correctly-labeled §12.3.1.1 immediately preceding it) requires TSCF-headed AVTPDUs to be dropped in HW_CONFIGURED without further response, unconditionally. lifecycle::should_accept now drops a TSCF-headed frame in HW_CONFIGURED regardless of time_sync_supported, the same unconditional rule already applied to HW_UNCONFIGURED. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-028; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops ACF_GBB-format requests without response
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (resolved differently than originally scoped): this entry's own remaining exposure -- a conditional (ACF_GBB) request literally addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED, the one case REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's byte_bus_id restriction did not already cover -- turned out to directly conflict with TC18 §12.7's own text once REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 was scoped: §12.7 requires EP0-addressed non-STANDARD requests to be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not silently dropped as this entry's own §12.3.1.2 citation demands. Resolved by reading §12.3.1.2's "requests in ACF_GBB format[are dropped]" as the general, non-EP0-scoped rule (still correctly enforced -- any non-EP0 byte_bus_id is dropped by REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's own restriction, unconditionally of acf_msg_type) and §12.7's REQUEST_REJECTED rule as the more specific, EP0-scoped override that governs for exactly this residual case. lifecycle::should_accept now returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_REJECT (not RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP) for a non-ABB message addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-033's own entry for the implementation detail, and that function's own header doc comment for the full reconciliation between the two TC18 sections. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-029; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state write is accepted only from the discovery stream, the root client, or (with no root client) any valid stream
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (issue #341 lineage): the missing classification this requirement's own former text named -- "a distinction this library cannot yet express (no wire-level concept of 'a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination' independent of a specific endpoint's own owning stream)" -- now exists. New rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_valid_association() (regmap.h/.c) is a direct membership query over TC18 §12.7.8 Table 25's own EP_ID_config table: true iff SOME row names the exact (request_stream_index, byte_bus_id) pair, regardless of which ep_id owns it -- the "regardless of which endpoint owns it" distinction is exactly what separates it from rcp_regmap_ep_client_t's own single-endpoint-scoped via_owning_stream. rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() now derives a new rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t member, via_valid_stream_association, from it -- bakes TC18's own "If a root client is configured only the root client's stream_id/byte_bus_id is accepted" narrowing directly into the member itself (map->svr_root_client_index == RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT AND a valid association), the same pattern via_root_client_ep0 already used for its own root-client-index check, so the member is always false by construction when a root client IS configured and can never wrongly widen access. lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition now ORs writer.via_valid_stream_association into its authorization check for both the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance and the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset -- the two transitions TC18 §12.3.1.2's identical wording governs -- but deliberately NOT into the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, which §12.7.4's own narrower text (REQ-LIFECYCLE-037) restricts to via_root_client_ep0 alone; a dedicated test (test_lifecycle.c) pins that this new member does not widen that specific reset. Mutation-tested: the OR-clause, the membership scan, and the "no root client configured" guard were each independently removed/weakened and confirmed to fail the new tests, then restored. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-031; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2, TC18.txt L2562-L2565 and L2574-L2577 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338). Line numbers corrected to the real current location in the refreshed RC5 TC18.txt; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, non-configuration requests to endpoints other than EP0 are dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no wire-level encode/decode pair for a functional-configuration read/write request at all, for any endpoint type -- regmap.h's own file header documents this as deliberately deferred ("wiring them to an actual byte_message_info read/write exchange is later phases' job"), confirmed by grepping the whole codebase for any regmap encode/decode pair and finding none outside discovery.c's own read-only discovery-response encoder. Every wire request this library can currently decode for a non-EP0 endpoint is therefore, by construction, operational -- so lifecycle::should_accept now restricts HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID (EP0) only, the honestly-achievable form of TC18 §12.3.1.2's "requests to EPs other than EP0 that are not config requests will be ignored and dropped without response" given this library's real current wire-format scope. Migrating this restriction into lifecycle::should_accept required moving test_mock.c's and test_conditional_dispatch.c's own dispatch fixtures from HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED (both files' fixtures dispatch to non-EP0 endpoints as their normal, unremarkable test setup, not gap-specific behavior). (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-032; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: Non-STANDARD requests to EP0 before full configuration must be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the RCP_SCHED_KIND_* input this entry's own text said was needed is unnecessary machinery -- STANDARD-vs-conditional is already fully determined by the acf_msg_type parameter lifecycle::should_accept already receives (ACF_ABB is this codebase's wire encoding for STANDARD requests; ACF_GBB is the encoding for every conditional request kind -- compound/compound-wait/triggered/chained/timed/cancel -- unconditionally, per request_compound.h and siblings' own mtv-repurposing scheme). Fixed: lifecycle::should_accept's bool return widened to a three-way rcp_lifecycle_accept_t (ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT); a non-ABB message type addressed to EP0 (RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID) while HW_UNCONFIGURED, or while HW_CONFIGURED (this library's own architecture makes TC18's "no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations have been defined" condition permanently true throughout HW_CONFIGURED, since no wire-level regmap read/write exists yet to ever establish one), now returns REJECT instead of the prior silent DROP. rcp_mock_server_dispatch() answers a REJECT with RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED (wire code 11) via the same rcp_acf_build_error_response() convention find_slot()'s own EP_NOT_FOUND path already used, and returns the pre-existing RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_REJECTED result. This also resolves REQ-LIFECYCLE-029's own residual (see that entry) by treating §12.7's EP0-scoped REJECT as the more specific rule overriding §12.3.1.2's general ACF_GBB-drop rule for exactly this case. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-033; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2827-2830

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the claimed discovery stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: the same underlying gap as REQ-LIFECYCLE-026 (this entry's own "claimed discovery stream" framing and that entry's "discovery claimant's stream" framing describe one code path, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED writability), closed by the same fix -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-026's own text for the full correction (the enforcement point is lifecycle::is_field_writable, not lifecycle::should_accept as originally assumed here too). rcp_discovery_claim_note_request()/rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) remain pure primitives a caller composes into writer.via_discovery_stream, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- unchanged by this fix, and correctly so. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-035; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.7.2 Configuration in HW_UNCONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2868-2870

requirements.title: Once RCP_CONFIGURED, a discovery request may no longer change configuration although it is still answered
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found this entry had actually conflated two different things -- lifecycle::is_field_writable's FUNCTIONAL_W RCP_CONFIGURED branch already correctly excluded via_discovery_stream before this fix (authorized there is via_root_client_ep0 || via_owning_stream only), so field WRITES were never actually leaking discovery-stream authority into RCP_CONFIGURED. The real, confirmed gap was in lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition's own RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset path: it shared one `authorized` (via_discovery_stream || via_root_client_ep0) computation with the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, so a bare discovery-stream writer could still demote a fully RCP_CONFIGURED server -- itself a configuration change TC18 §12.7.4's "Changes in configuration via a discovery request are no longer allowed" forbids. Fixed: the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset now requires writer.via_root_client_ep0 specifically (the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset keeps the wider rule, since §12.7.3 still permits the discovery stream while HW_CONFIGURED). rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write()/rcp_discovery_claim_release() (src/discovery.c) remain pure claim-bookkeeping primitives that deliberately do not consult lifecycle state, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the claim primitive still refreshes for the claimant regardless of state, but that no longer translates into actual write or transition authority once RCP_CONFIGURED, since both real gates (field_writable() and transition()) now independently close that door. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-037; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.7.4 Configuration in RCP_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2876-2879

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT's own third plausibility bullet -- every configured request stream has at least one endpoint using it
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): TC18 §12.3.1.2's RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT plausibility check names three bullets for the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED transition: (1) "Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-005/007; (2) "For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured" -- the mirror-image completeness check, that no request stream is left configured with zero endpoints actually using it; (3) "Each response stream configured is assigned to at least one request stream" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-006. Bullet 2 previously had no counterpart in lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg: rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t carried only `configured` and `has_response_stream`, with no field representing whether any endpoint actually referenced that specific stream, so a request stream marked `configured = true` with zero endpoints bound to it -- an orphaned, unused stream slot -- passed the check exactly as if it were legitimately in use. Fixed by adding a new `request_stream_index` field to rcp_lifecycle_endpoint_plausibility_t (placed as the struct's own last field so existing positional-initializer call sites keep compiling, matching this codebase's established backward-compatibility convention) and a new bullet-2 scan in lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg that, for each configured request stream, requires at least one endpoint with `ep_used && has_stream_assoc && request_stream_index == i`. Mutation-testing during this fix caught a genuine correctness gap in the first draft: the bullet-2 scan did not check `ep_used`, so a stale/unused endpoint slot (skipped by bullet 1's own loop, its `has_stream_assoc`/`request_stream_index` never validated by anything) could incorrectly "cover" an otherwise-orphaned stream if it happened to carry leftover `has_stream_assoc = true` and a matching index; the `ep_used` guard was added and a dedicated test (`test_rcp_cfg_inconsistent_an_unused_endpoint_does_not_cover_a_stream`) added to discriminate it. 5 tests (1 rewritten gap-pinning test, 4 new), 3/3 systematic mutations caught cleanly after the fix. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-038; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced. Plausibility check contains a check that: ... For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured ... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2566-2572

requirements.title: RCP_CONFIGURED to HW_CONFIGURED demotion is gated by EP0 writer authorization and idleness
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-16 (issue #455): TC18 Figure 17 explicitly diagrams a direct RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED arrow -- "Root Client or (stream/bb_ID & no root configured) access via EP0 to set state to HW_CONFIGURED & all other EPs are Idle -> send positive response" -- that lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition previously did not implement at all: this specific (from, target) pair fell through unconditionally to the function's own catch-all, returning RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION regardless of writer or idleness, even though the diagram models it as a real, first-class demotion (confirmed via a pixel-level re-transcription of the diagram, page 51 of the current RC5 PDF -- the arrow's own arrowhead terminates on HW_CONFIGURED's boundary, tail on RCP_CONFIGURED's). Now implemented as a dedicated branch in lifecycle::RcServerState::try_transition: authorized only via writer.via_root_client_ep0 or writer.via_valid_stream_association (both are, by the label's own text, "access via EP0" -- via_discovery_stream is deliberately NOT accepted, consistent with REQ-LIFECYCLE-037's own finding that the discovery stream no longer authorizes a configuration change once already RCP_CONFIGURED), then gated by all_other_eps_idle (RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE otherwise, see REQ-LIFECYCLE-022). No plausibility recheck -- a demotion, like the other two reset paths (REQ-LIFECYCLE-010/011), does not re-verify configuration consistency. REQ-LIFECYCLE-012's own "unmodeled transitions" list corrected accordingly (previously, incorrectly, named this pair as an example of a rejected transition). (Ported from c-RCP REQ-LIFECYCLE-039; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2492-L2495 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517; page 51 of OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf) -- verified directly against the primary-source PDF image at pixel resolution (not just the pre-existing text extraction, which loses the diagram's own arrow topology), independently of issue #455's own initial report.

requirements.title: lifecycle::should_accept honors the IGNORE policy for a TSCF-without-time-sync frame (§13.3)
requirements.text: lifecycle::should_accept shall accept the same unsupported_time_sync_policy parameter and, at RCP_CONFIGURED (the only state whose own TSCF admission is governed solely by this general time-sync check), shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPT rather than RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP for a TSCF-headed request received while server_time_sync_supported is false and unsupported_time_sync_policy equals RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_IGNORE. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-AVTP-029; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("Requests may come within an AVTPDU with a presentation time (i.e. TSCF header). In case the RC Server does not support time synchronization, the presentation time shall be ignored, and the request(s) executed as if no presentation time were included or dropped depending on the configuration of the RC Server."), TC18.txt L4035-4038

requirements.title: lifecycle::check_field_writable distinguishes LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (state-locked) from UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (writer-denied)
requirements.text: lifecycle::check_field_writable shall return RCP_ERROR_NONE when rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, kind, writer) is true; RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS when the denial is state-driven (a maximally-privileged writer for the same state/kind would also be denied) -- the code closest in meaning to TC18 Figure 17's own diagram-only "LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS" transition, which names no numbered wire error code exactly but unambiguously matches LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (4), the only numbered code with a semantically corresponding name; and RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS when the denial is specific to this writer or frame on top of an otherwise-permitting state -- TC18 §13.7.1.2's own separate, narrower concrete example (REQ-LIFECYCLE-024). CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (issue #455, citation-drift fix, same lineage as the 2026-08-13 pass on REQ-DISC-029/LIFECYCLE-022/024/025): this entry's own citation previously said "Figure 16", stale after the RC5 renumbering -- the lifecycle diagram is Figure 17 in the current RC5 baseline; the underlying technical claim is unchanged. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-WIREERR-004; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 ("Writing to a write prohibited register (e.g. lock bit for map set) creates a response with err = 1 and an error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS"), TC18.txt L4436-4437; §12.9.6 Table 30 (UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS=3, LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS=4), TC18.txt L3815-3816; Figure 17's LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS transition, cross-referencing REQ-LIFECYCLE-024's own citation for the state-locked case

requirements.title: request stream's response-stream pointer and its discovery-enabling default of 1 (rx_resp_stream_index)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_resp_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x0011, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their responses, with 0 meaning "no response is to be sent". FIXED: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_init() now sets this one field to 1 (not 0), reproducing the specification's own bootstrap guarantee that a freshly reset server can answer a discovery request before any configuration has been written -- REQ-RMAP-018's own text was corrected to carve out this deliberate exception to its "zero everything" rule. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the identical wire codec now serves this field too; a client can now write AND read rx_resp_stream_index over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the write dispatcher now enforces this table's own FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR access type before applying any write, including to this field. PLAUSIBILITY-VALIDATION HALF CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): lifecycle::check_rcp_cfg's own RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT check previously only checked a boolean has_response_stream (src/lifecycle.c), which recorded that SOME response stream exists but not which one. rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t now carries a caller-supplied response_stream_index field, validated against a new response_stream_count on the snapshot (rcp_lifecycle_plausibility_snapshot_t) -- the same request_stream_index/request_stream_count cross-reference convention REQ-LIFECYCLE-038 already established one level up. STILL PARTIAL: no code path yet routes a live response to the selected stream from this field at runtime (the ack-routing half) -- that is a genuinely separate, still-open gap about runtime behavior consuming the field, not about wire reachability or plausibility validation, and (per project decision 2026-08-13) is left documented rather than built out in this pass. RUNTIME CONSUMPTION CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): see REQ-RMAP-048's own text -- the identical suppress_response_per_stream_cfg() wiring (mock.c) now also governs this field: a built response classified as anything OTHER than Acknowledge (Write/Read/Error -- everything mock.c's own dispatch pipeline actually produces today) is suppressed when rx_resp_stream_index == 0 for the resolved stream, exercised end to end through rcp_mock_server_dispatch() itself with a real ACF_ABB-encoded request/response pair, not merely by reading the struct field directly. An unresolvable stream_id (no rcp_mock_server_set_request_stream_cfg() call for it) suppresses nothing, matching every other fail-toward-no-action resolve_index() call site in mock.c; rx_resp_stream_index's own nonzero default (REQ-RMAP-049's own earlier fix) means every pre-existing test in this codebase that never configures a request stream, or that configures one and leaves this field at its default, is completely unaffected -- confirmed by a full, unmodified 66-test-suite pass before any new test was added. The suppression condition was mutation-tested and caught cleanly. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (issue #458): unaffected in its own right (relative address 0x0011, a different octet entirely) -- flagged only because it shares this same Table 24 row with the 0x000D octet REQ-RMAP-051's own text reconciles. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-RMAP-049; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: the W+ lockable access type for EP_ID_config and the Table 27 W+ queue fields
requirements.text: lifecycle::is_field_writable_w_plus/_write_error_w_plus() (lifecycle.h/lifecycle.c) implement TC18's W+ (explicitly lockable) register access type -- EP_ID_config rows (§12.7.8 Table 25) and the STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time queue registers (§12.7.9 Table 27) are both marked R/W+: the table may be locked by the configuring instance to protect against unwanted later modification, independently of the lifecycle state that governs W and W*. Deliberately a SEPARATE function rather than a new rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t value threaded through lifecycle::is_field_writable's own signature -- that function has roughly 90 existing call sites across every endpoint type, 2 internal uses, and every test exercising any of them, none of which need a lock concept; a standalone function delivers the same primitive with zero blast radius to existing callers, reusing (not re-deriving) the existing FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR state/writer rule internally. WIRED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now calls this primitive for both tables before applying any write -- EP_ID_config's whole row via lifecycle::is_field_writable_w_plus directly against svr_configuration_lock, and Table 27's own mixed-field row via the new respqueue_cfg_row_write_authorize() helper, which classifies each touched octet's row-relative offset and requires the W+ variant to authorize whenever a write touches STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time. This closes the register-map write path this entry's own prior text called missing -- a client can now actually latch either table over the wire, subject to this authorization. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-RMAP-055; c-RCP function names map to their rust ports in src/lifecycle.rs.)

requirements.title: Every register in the RC Server static part (General block) is read-only to a remote client
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 marks every register of the RC Server general (static) part with access type R; a remote write to any of them must not take effect. lifecycle::is_field_writable models this as FieldKind::ReadOnly: unwritable in every lifecycle state by every writer, and lifecycle::check_field_writable reports RcpError::LockedMemAccess for it (never UnauthorizedAccess). lifecycle::lock_policy maps RegisterCategory::General to None. regmap::general_decode_write_request recognizes an ACF_ABB WRITE addressed to EP0 and always reports LockedMemAccess with the request transaction_num, and mock::RcServer::handle_abb rejects every EP0 General write with LockedMemAccess for any writer, root client included, without modifying the GeneralRegisters snapshot. (Ported from c-RCP REQ-RMAP-025, whose ID is already used in rust-RCP.)

requirements.title: encode_compound_request() packs the step at the specification's own sub-field offsets
requirements.text: encode_compound_request() shall, given a recognized request_type and payload_len <= the ACF 9-bit quadlet range, produce an ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN + payload_len byte frame of type ACF_GBB_MSG_TYPE addressed to byte_bus_id with mtv forced to 0, and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step.start_state at offset 1, step.next_state at offset 2, step.sequencer_index at offset 3, step.exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step.repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.2 Figure 8 / Table 7, §11.2.2.3 Figure 9 / Table 8). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1494-1506

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a frame shorter than declared
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall return RequestCodecError::ShortFrame when b is shorter than the ACF_GBB fixed header or its declared payload length. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a non-ACF_GBB message
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall return RequestCodecError::BadMsgType when (b[0] >> 1) != ACF_GBB_MSG_TYPE (the acf_msg_type field packed into b[0]'s bits 7:1). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a message whose mtv is not untimed
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall return RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the decoded byte_message_info.mtv is not mtv = 0. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a request_type it does not recognize
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte is neither a compound kind nor a compound-wait kind. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("first byte in message_timestamp field" -> "type of condition": 0x0F/0x8F Compound, 0x0B/0x8B Compound wait), TC18.txt L1254-1267

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() recovers every sub-field from the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall, given a frame whose repurposed message_timestamp region carries the layout REQ-CMP-010 defines, return Ok and recover request_type, byte_bus_id, transaction_num, and every CompoundStep sub-field (start_state, next_state, sequencer_index, exec_delay, repeat_count) from those same offsets and widths, with sequencer_index one octet wide and repeat_count two octets wide. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1494-1506

requirements.title: encode_clear_non_safestate() encodes an ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN-byte, opcode-0x06, mtv-untimed frame
requirements.text: encode_clear_non_safestate() shall produce an ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN-byte frame of type ACF_GBB_MSG_TYPE addressed to byte_bus_id, echoing transaction_num, with mtv mtv = 0 and the message_timestamp region's leading byte equal to RequestKind::ClearNonSafestate and its remaining 7 bytes zero. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L2093-2124

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() round-trips a frame produced by its own encoder
requirements.text: decode_clear_non_safestate() shall, given a frame produced by encode_clear_non_safestate(), return Ok and recover the original byte_bus_id and transaction_num. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Figure 15 (clear-non-safestate GBB layout), TC18.txt L2073-2082

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a request_type other than 0x06
requirements.text: decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte is not RequestKind::ClearNonSafestate, given the same short-frame/bad-msg-type/not-repurposed failure modes as decode_compound_request(). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L2093-2124

requirements.title: encode_compound_request() packs evt into the shared byte_message_info header, not one of step's repurposed sub-fields
requirements.text: encode_compound_request() shall write its evt parameter into the encoded frame's byte_message_info.evt field (Table 4 octet 4 bits 7:4) via the ACF byte_message_info encoder, independently of every CompoundStep sub-field packed into the repurposed message_timestamp region. For a compound-wait request this is the TC18 §13.5.1 comparison-mode selector; a plain compound request has no comparison of its own. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() surfaces the decoded byte_message_info.evt field
requirements.text: decode_compound_request() shall, on Ok, populate the decoded evt with the decoded byte_message_info.evt field, independently of every recovered CompoundStep sub-field. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-non-safestate carries no sub-field of its own. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): the decode function previously read only the leading request_type byte and never validated the remaining 7 octets TC18 Table 14 marks reserved. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L2093-2097

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestCodecError::EvtHsCsNonzero when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero, per TC18 Table 14's explicit prose ("evt[2:0], hs, cs: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"). Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this ACF-header-level field was entirely unvalidated before this milestone -- Table 14 is the only one of the three cancel-family tables (13/14/15) to name a specific TC18 Table 30 wire error code for this violation, which a caller wiring this into a real response should reuse (RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD, errors.h) rather than inventing its own mapping. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 ("evt[2:0], hs, cs: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L2118-2124

requirements.title: decode_triggered_request() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: decode_triggered_request() shall return RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the decoded mtv is not mtv = 0. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_triggered_request() rejects a non-triggered opcode and otherwise recovers every sub-field
requirements.text: decode_triggered_request() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte does not satisfy a triggered kind, and shall otherwise populate the decoded request_type, the decoded byte_bus_id, the decoded transaction_num, a borrowed the decoded payload/the decoded payload_len view, and every TriggeredStep sub-field from the offsets and widths REQ-TRIG-004 defines. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("0x0E, 0x8E" -> "Triggered"), TC18.txt L1254-1267

requirements.title: TriggeredRuntime::enter_started() resets the trigger-occurrence counter
requirements.text: TriggeredRuntime::enter_started() shall set occurrence_count to 0 and started to true. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695

requirements.title: TriggeredRuntime::record_occurrence() counts only the trigger this request selected
requirements.text: TriggeredRuntime::record_occurrence() shall increment runtime.occurrence_count and return true iff runtime.started is true and the observed occurrence matches this request's own selection, i.e. source_ep == step.trigger_source_ep and signal_nr == step.trigger_signal_nr. It shall leave the runtime entirely unchanged and return false for an occurrence from any other endpoint or any other trigger signal number, and for any occurrence while runtime.started is false (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_source_ep defines the endpoint which issues the trigger... trigger_signal_nr defines the trigger number of the endpoint addressed by trigger_source_ep"), TC18.txt L1720-1721

requirements.title: TriggeredRuntime::threshold_reached() counts occurrences that must precede execution
requirements.text: TriggeredRuntime::threshold_reached() shall return true iff runtime.occurrence_count > step.trigger_threshold, so that a trigger_threshold of zero is satisfied by one occurrence and a trigger_threshold of N by N+1 occurrences, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8 ("'0' results in execution after one trigger signal while a '3' will cause an execution after four occurrences"). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_threshold), TC18.txt L1722-1724

requirements.title: TriggeredStep::exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against exec_delay
requirements.text: TriggeredStep::exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= step.exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8), not in milliseconds. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_exec_delay), TC18.txt L1725-1727

requirements.title: TriggeredRuntime::tick() only fires when started, the threshold is reached, the delay has elapsed, and the endpoint is idle
requirements.text: TriggeredRuntime::tick() shall return false and leave the runtime unchanged unless runtime.started is true, TriggeredRuntime::threshold_reached(step) holds, TriggeredStep::exec_delay_elapsed(elapsed) holds, and endpoint_idle is true. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; "When the trigger_exec_delay timer has expired the state advances to RE as soon as the EP is idle and no request with higher priority is pending.", TC18.txt L3692-3693

requirements.title: TriggeredRuntime::tick() resets the runtime on a successful fire and advances no sequencer
requirements.text: When every condition REQ-TRIG-012 names holds, TriggeredRuntime::tick() shall reset runtime.occurrence_count to 0 and runtime.started to false and return true. It shall not read or write any sequencer state: a triggered request carries no sequencer, start_state, or next_state sub-field (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Table 8). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; TC18.txt L3692-3693 (trigger_exec_delay expiry + EP-idle gating)

requirements.title: encode_chained_member() packs chain_exec_delay and cs at the specification's own positions
requirements.text: For valid inputs, encode_chained_member() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to 0, the opcode byte RequestKind::Chained at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, chain_exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and cs encoded into byte_message_info's own cs bit (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Figure 11 / Table 9). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 Table 11 (chain_exec_delay, cs semantics), TC18.txt L1828-1839

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() maps ACF decode failures to their RequestCodecError equivalents
requirements.text: decode_chained_member() shall return RequestCodecError::ShortFrame or RequestCodecError::BadMsgType when the ACF_GBB decoder reports the corresponding failure. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: decode_chained_member() shall return RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the decoded mtv is not mtv = 0. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-chained opcode and otherwise recovers chain_exec_delay and cs
requirements.text: decode_chained_member() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte is not RequestKind::Chained, and shall otherwise populate the decoded byte_bus_id, the decoded chain_exec_delay (from offsets 4-5), the decoded cs, the decoded transaction_num, and a borrowed the decoded payload/the decoded payload_len view. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-zero reserved sub-field octet
requirements.text: decode_chained_member() shall return RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero when any of octets 1-3 or 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries a set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.4 Table 9. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request will be rejected" / "...shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L1827, L1830

requirements.title: encode_timed_request() packs a 48-bit presentation_time and holds the reserved octet at zero
requirements.text: encode_timed_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to 0, hs and cs clear, the opcode byte RequestKind::Timed at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, an all-zero reserved octet at offset 1, and presentation_time as six big-endian octets spanning offsets 2-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Figure 12 / Table 10). It shall return an Err, never a truncated frame, when presentation_time exceeds TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Figure 13 (48-bit presentation_time offset), TC18.txt L1871-1882

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: decode_timed_request() shall return RequestCodecError::ShortFrame or RequestCodecError::BadMsgType when the ACF_GBB decoder reports the corresponding failure, and RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the decoded mtv is not mtv = 0. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a non-timed opcode and otherwise recovers the 48-bit presentation_time
requirements.text: decode_timed_request() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte is not RequestKind::Timed, and shall otherwise populate the decoded byte_bus_id, the decoded transaction_num, a borrowed the decoded payload/the decoded payload_len view, and the decoded presentation_time from the six octets at offsets 2-7 of the repurposed region, in [0, TIMED_PRESENTATION_TIME_MAX]. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a non-zero reserved octet
requirements.text: decode_timed_request() shall return RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero when the reserved octet at offset 1 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries any set bit, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Table 12 (reserved bits must be 0), TC18.txt L1906

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a timed request with hs or cs set
requirements.text: decode_timed_request() shall return RequestCodecError::UnsupportedCmd when the decoded byte_message_info hs or cs bit is set, per TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("hs, cs -- All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Table 12 (hs and cs shall both be 0b), TC18.txt L1911-1912

requirements.title: encode_clear_single() packs clear_transaction_num at the specification's own offset
requirements.text: encode_clear_single() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to 0, the opcode byte RequestKind::ClearSingle at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, clear_transaction_num at octet offset 3, and octets 1-2 and 4-7 all-zero (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.3.3 Figure 16 / Table 15). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 16 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num offset), TC18.txt L2140-2158

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: decode_clear_single() shall return RequestCodecError::ShortFrame or RequestCodecError::BadMsgType when the ACF_GBB decoder reports the corresponding failure, and RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the decoded mtv is not mtv = 0. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 16 / Table 15 (Usage of GBB message to cancel a single, specific request, request_type=0x07, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L2140-2210; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis and §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() recovers clear_transaction_num from the specification's own offset
requirements.text: decode_clear_single() shall return RequestCodecError::UnknownType when the decoded opcode byte is not RequestKind::ClearSingle, RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero when any of octets 1-2 or 4-7 of the repurposed region carries a set bit, and shall otherwise populate the decoded byte_bus_id, the decoded transaction_num, and the decoded clear_transaction_num from octet offset 3. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Table 15 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L2185

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: decode_clear_all() shall return RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-all carries no sub-field of its own. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): the decode function previously read only the leading request_type byte and never validated the remaining 7 octets TC18 Table 13 marks reserved. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 13 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L2025

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: decode_clear_all() shall return RequestCodecError::EvtHsCsNonzero when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero -- TC18 Table 13 defines only evt = 0000b (no ack) or 1000b (ack requested) as valid, meaning evt[2:0] must be zero, and both hs and cs are documented as always 0b. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this ACF-header-level field was entirely unvalidated by any of the three cancel-family decode functions before this milestone. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 13 (evt/hs/cs field descriptions), TC18.txt L2026-2030

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: decode_clear_single() shall return RequestCodecError::EvtHsCsNonzero when the decoded ACF byte_message_info header's evt[2:0], hs, or cs is nonzero, per TC18 Table 15's explicit prose ("Evt, hs and cs shall be zero") -- the same rule as REQ-CANCEL-014's clear-all case, applied to clear-single. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H). Distinct from REQ-CANCEL-007's own RequestCodecError::ReservedNonzero check, which validates message_timestamp's own reserved octets, a different wire region from the ACF header's evt/hs/cs bits. Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("Evt, hs and cs shall be zero"), Table 15, TC18.txt L2140-2185

requirements.title: peek_request_type() reads the repurposed opcode byte of an untimed ACF_GBB frame
requirements.text: peek_request_type(b) shall return RequestCodecError::ShortFrame when b is shorter than ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN, RequestCodecError::BadMsgType when b[0] >> 1 != ACF_GBB_MSG_TYPE, RequestCodecError::NotRepurposed when the mtv bit is set, and otherwise Ok(b[ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN]) (c-RCP rcp_compound_peek_request_type(), REQ-CMP-005..007 there); never panics.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: encode_compound_request() rejects a non-compound request kind
requirements.text: encode_compound_request() shall return Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when request_type is not one of RequestKind::Compound, SafetyCompound, CompoundWait, SafetyCompoundWait (c-RCP rcp_compound_encode_request() returns a NULL frame, REQ-CMP-008 there).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1379-1458; §11.2.2.3 Table 8 / Figure 9 (GBB message for compound wait requests: request_type, cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay, cmpw_repetitions), TC18.txt L1476-1567

requirements.title: Conditional-request encoders reject an oversized payload
requirements.text: encode_compound_request() (and every other conditional-request encoder) shall return Err(RcpError::InvalidSize) when the payload does not fit the ACF 9-bit acf_msg_length quadlet range (more than 2028 octets for ACF_GBB), or when byte_bus_id exceeds 11 bits (c-RCP returns a NULL frame for payload_len > RCP_ACF_GBB_MAX_PAYLOAD, REQ-CMP-009 there).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1379-1458; §11.2.2.3 Table 8 / Figure 9 (GBB message for compound wait requests: request_type, cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay, cmpw_repetitions), TC18.txt L1476-1567

requirements.title: RequestCodecError gives each decode failure a distinct message and sends no response
requirements.text: RequestCodecError shall give every variant (ShortFrame, BadMsgType, NotRepurposed, UnknownType, ReservedNonzero, EvtHsCsNonzero, UnsupportedCmd) a distinct, non-empty Display message (c-RCP rcp_*_strerror(), REQ-CMP-004/TRIG-002/CHAIN-001/TIMED-001/CANCEL-001 there), and RequestCodecError::response_error() shall return None for every variant: c-RCP parity (c-RCP src/server.c:458-512, src/mock.c:1198) -- a conditional request whose body fails to decode is rejected with no error response, diverging from TC18 RC5's rejected-with-error-code wording.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: complete_repetition() applies the cmp/cmpw/trigger_repetitions end-of-execution rule
requirements.text: complete_repetition(&mut repeat_count) shall leave the infinite sentinel 0xFFFF unchanged and return true (request stays stored), return false for 0 (request removed from the endpoint request storage), and otherwise decrement by one and return true (c-RCP rcp_server_endpoint_complete(), src/server.c:875-883).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_repetitions ... If the field has a zero at the end of the execution, the request will be removed from the EP request storage, otherwise decreased by one."), TC18.txt L1724-1728

requirements.title: encode_triggered_request() packs the trigger-selection sub-fields at the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: For a recognized request_type, encode_triggered_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to 0 and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step.trigger_source_ep at offset 1, step.trigger_signal_nr at offset 2, step.trigger_threshold at offset 3, step.exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step.repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7 (TC18 v0.5.1_RC §11.2.2.3 Figure 10 / Table 8). Ported from c-RCP src/request.c; byte-for-byte parity proven against golden vectors generated from c-RCP's librcp.a. (REQ-TRIG-004 in c-RCP.)
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1720-1721

requirements.title: encode_triggered_request() rejects a non-triggered request kind
requirements.text: encode_triggered_request() shall return Err(RcpError::InvalidParameter) when request_type is neither RequestKind::Triggered nor RequestKind::SafetyTriggered (c-RCP returns a NULL frame, REQ-TRIG-003 there).
